News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

News.title: Antonelli walks on water while Hamilton rages from mountaintop
News.content:
The 20-year-old also benefited from a perfectly-timed (from his perspective at least) mid-race virtual safety car when Lance Stroll retired his Aston Martin, which allowed Antonelli a cheap stop to switch to fresh mediums while Russell stayed out on used hards. But at some point you just have to take your hat off to the youngster.

Antonelli was irresistible. He had already surged from 19th on the grid to 12th by the time the red flag came out at the end of lap 2. He was up to sixth a couple of laps after the race resumed. And by lap 18 of a 53-lap race, he had passed Russell for the lead for the first time. That is some going.

Having caught up to Russell, the two Mercedes drivers engaged in an entertaining battle for a few laps, the pair of them yo-yoing in and out of the lead before Russell got past Antonelli on lap 23 and managed to make it stick.

But the key moment of the race came on lap 27 when Stroll stopped at the first chicane and the VSC came out. For Antonelli, the decision to switch to fresh mediums was clear. He was going to struggle to make it to the end of the race. Far better to drop a few positions and fight back on fresh rubber.

For Russell, it was far trickier. He was in the lead of the race. He was on hard tyres which he knew could get to the end of the race. And he also had the problem of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who at the time he was struggling to shake off.

Mercedes chose to keep Russell out there. In hindsight, it may have been the wrong decision. Had he stopped at that point, he would at least have stayed ahead of Antonelli, and on the same tyres. By staying out, he kept the lead but found himself relentlessly hunted down by the Italian.

By lap 49, the Italian had caught up to him. Antonelli botched his first attempt at reclaiming the lead, going wide onto the gravel at the first chicane. But he made no mistake one lap later as Russell was once again left licking his wounds.

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Sports.title: Aston Villa attack clicks in thrilling win over Club Brugge
Sports.content:
Aston Villa produced a superb attacking display to end their scoring concerns and begin their Champions League campaign with a thrilling 3-2 win over Club Brugge.

The Europa League winners had failed to score in their first three Premier League matches, having had just one shot on target, but their attack clicked in Belgium as John McGinn, Emiliano Buendia and Nicolas Jackson struck to kickstart their season.

Villa had 14 efforts in a scintillating first-half performance that began with McGinn expertly side-footing a trademark first-time shot into the bottom left corner after being set up by Pau Torres' driving run out of defence.

Club Brugge's expansive approach contributed to a breathless tie and the hosts equalised when Hugo Vetlesen swept a low shot into the corner, although Buendia restored Villa's lead within three minutes, tapping in from close range following good work by Joao Gomes.

Villa threatened constantly on the counter-attack and their third goal came when Jackson ran in behind to try and latch onto Torres' long ball forward, beating goalkeeper Yann Sommer to the ball and slotting into an empty net for his first goal since joining in a club-record £65m move.

The hosts pulled one back just after the hour mark through Nicolo Tresoldi's penalty, awarded for handball on Aaron Wan-Bissaka after the referee was sent to the pitchside monitor, but despite coming under heavy pressure, Villa held on for victory.

11: GOAL! McGinn scores Villa's first goal of the season with a lovely side-footed finish.

19: EQUALISER! Vetlesen produces his inner McGinn by slotting the ball into the bottom right corner.

22: VILLA LEAD AGAIN! The hosts are level for just three minutes as Buendia arrives to tap-in from close range after good work from Gomes.

43: JACKSON SCORES! The striker caps Villa's superb attacking performance by beating Sommer to the ball and slotting into an open net.

61: GOAL! Game on as Tresoldi slots away a penalty after Wan-Bissaka's handball.

69: WOODWORK! Emery makes three subs before Villa are about to defend a corner and then Tresoldi's glancing header at the set piece is pushed onto the post by Suzuki.

82: OFF THE LINE! Bogarde is denied from wrapping up the win for Villa as his shot is cleared.

Sports.title: Sabalenka survives Noskova battle to keep US Open three-peat bid alive
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka maintained her hopes of a third successive US Open title with a three-set victory over Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in an absorbing quarter-final - a result that retains her status as world No 1 for at least one more day.

The 28-year-old beat Noskova 7-6 (7-1) 3-6 7-6 (10-7), coming through two tie-breaks - and a 4-2 deficit in the final set - as she sealed victory with a second-serve ace to set up a meeting with the winner of Tuesday night's all-American clash between Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro in the semi-finals.

Sabalenka needs to win in New York to have any hope of staying as world No 1 but will definitely lose that spot if Elena Rybakina - who defeated Sabalenka in this year's Australian Open final - overcomes Qinwen Zheng in her quarter-final on Wednesday.

If Rybakina is beaten, then Pegula or Coco Gauff could rise to the top of the rankings should they win the tournament at Flushing Meadows on Saturday evening.

Image: Sabalenka is aiming to win a third straight US Open title

Sabalenka, world No 1 for 99 consecutive weeks, is hoping to become the first woman to win the US Open three times in a row since Serena Williams from 2012-14.

Noskova, who had forced a first-set tie-break from 5-2 down, double faulted at 3-3 in the final-set breaker and then slipped 8-6 down after an unfortunate net cord, before Sabalenka, who has never lost a US Open quarter-final and won her last 10 tie-breaks at the event, edged into the last four.

Sabalenka extended her career record over Noskova to 3-0 after previously seeing off the 21-year-old in the Adelaide International final in 2023 and then the Indian Wells semi-finals earlier this year.

Noskova will not become the first woman to secure back-to-back Grand Slams since Naomi Osaka claimed the 2020 US Open and 2021 Australian Open after seeing her 11-match winning streak in majors come to an end.

Image: Noskova was hoping to become the first back-to-back Grand Slam winner since Naomi Osaka in 2021

Sabalenka: I thought the match was over

Aryna Sabalenka, speaking in her on-court interview:

"Thinking the match is over is probably what helped me to feel loose, go for my shots. I am super happy to get this win - a tough match, tough battle.

"These kind of crowds, tie-breaks, and these matches that are such high pressure boost my confidence and my energy.

"For now I just want to relax, recover, and reflect on what happened."

How Sabalenka fought past Noskova

Sabalenka broke Noskova to love in the second game of the match en route to a 5-2 lead, only to the lose four of the next five games as her Czech opponent fought back to 6-6.

Image: Sabalenka has never lost a US Open quarter-final

The first-set tie-break, however, was completely one-sided with Noskova's only point coming via an ace out wide as her double fault and Sabalenka's power settled things.

Noskova staved off break points early in the second set, including in the first game, and carved out two of her own on the Sabelanka serve at 3-2 up, taking the second of those when her rival produced an untimely double fault.

Sabalenka saved break point with an ace in her subsequent service game before Noskova went on to set up a deciding set by converting a fourth set point.

Noskova became the favourite when she broke Sabalenka for a 3-2 lead in the third set, with the world No 1 twice double-faulting in the game. But Sabalenka dug deep to level the match at 4-4 before the enthralled spectators were treated to another tie-break.

The second breaker was far more competitive than the first but Sabalenka came out on the right side of it once again to stay on course for a three-peat.

Henman: Sabalenka comes up with the big shots

Image: Sabalenka has held onto her No 1 world ranking for at least one more day

Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman:

"Some of her [bad form] has been in lesser tournaments, where her intensity and concentration hasn't been quite as good.

"But when you face someone the quality of your opponent, you have to stand and deliver.

"Her tie-break record is absolutely phenomenal - when it comes to the most pressure-packed moments, she's the one that comes up with the big shots."

Sports.title: 'Most pressure in the NFL' Finally Allen's time to win Super Bowl?
Sports.content:
Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady is under the most pressure in the NFL as he seeks to lead Josh Allen's side from 'bridesmaid to bride', says Sky Sports' Phoebe Schecter.

The Bills renew their Super Bowl quest this season having endured more playoff agony earlier this year when they were beaten by the Denver Broncos in overtime of January's Divisional Round clash.

It had been deemed a premature end to one of their best opportunities yet to end prolonged Super Bowl agony, with Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs absent from the playoffs for the first time since 2014 and the likes of Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow also nowhere to be seen.

Sean McDermott was subsequently fired after nine campaigns in charge, with Brady being promoted to head coach from his post as offensive coordinator.

"Josh Allen will have had a say with Joe Brady coming in and taking on that role," said former Bills coach Schecter on Inside the Huddle.

"It was just odd at the time in terms of how it happened, that kind of firing in order to promote from within."

Allen's Bills have suffered four Divisional Round exits and two AFC Championship Game defeats since 2020, four of those losses coming against the Chiefs.

Their 73 victories in that period are notably more than any other team in the league, Allen consistently spearheading one of football's most potent offenses.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Inside The Huddle podcast Neil Reynolds, Jeff Reinebold and Phoebe Schecter give their predictions on who will make the Super Bowl in 2027

Buffalo sought to strengthen their quarterback's aerial options by trading for Chicago Bears wide receiver DJ Moore, who hasn't recorded a 1,000-yard campaign since 2023.

"You look at what DJ Moore does for the team when you bring him in," Schecter continued. "That already elevates an offense that has never really had a star receiver.

"They're still trying to keep that mentality, but you pair that with a fantastic running game. We saw James Cook all last season taking over, but it's a very interesting that we have so many teams in the AFC that were having a similar conversation around with your Lamar Jacksons, your Joe Burrows - when will these guys win a Super Bowl?

"That of all the teams the most pressure is on Joe Brady in terms of the expectation is for him to get to a Super Bowl because they've always been the bridesmaid, never the bride.

"It'll be fascinating to see how he manages that pressure, especially as they move deeper into the season. But everyone feels good about it. You've got a new stadium, you've got a new excitement around it and that kind of rejuvenation."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Inside The Huddle podcast, Neil Reynolds and Jeff Reinebold discuss what a Patrick Mahomes return would look like after tearing his knee ligaments in December

The Bills also hired Jim Leonhard as their new defensive coordinator to oversee a new-look unit that saw the likes of Joey Bosa, AJ Epenesa, Matt Milano and Tre'Davious White depart in the offseason.

"Leonard is the key to this whole deal," said Sky Sports NFL's Jeff Reinebold. "Jim Leonard is a brilliant young coach, and if he can get that defense just a little bit better than it's been and better balance, this could be Buffalo's year."

Is this Burrow's time?

Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals stake their only claim as NFL 'nearly men' alongside both Allen's Bills and Jackson's Baltimore Ravens.

The Bengals have missed out on the playoffs for three straight years and managed just one postseason appearance since their defeat to the Los Angeles Rams at Super Bowl LVI.

Burrow, who has missed 16 games through injury over the last three seasons, demanded urgency from his team this offseason as he seeks to maximise, when healthy, one of the most explosive passing attacks in football.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jeff Reinebold and Phoebe Schecter discuss the prospect of Myles Garrett to the LA Rams and if he can lead them to Super Bowl glory

"He said it himself, we all know he's been injured so many times coming into this season, or they've had some big injury within the team, but the time is now and they've got to chase that success," said Schecter.

"The biggest complaint last year was how they were putting so much money into this defense and they were probably the worst performing defense.

"But bringing in Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, you get Kyle Dugger from the Patriots, you've got a smart defense. You've got a safety who can now organise everybody.

"They've got to be able to go down and capitalise on having this fantastic trio on offense with Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and go attack it. This city needs it.

"The fan base are so desperate for it and you don't have an endless clock with Joe Burrow, especially seeing his injury rate over the past few seasons."

Sports.title: Real Madrid v Inter, Millwall v Newcastle: Champions League and Carabao Cup – live
Sports.content:
2m ago 15.41 EDT Excellent work from Jones inside the Madrid box, back to goal. After good work from Lautaro and Augusto, he feints one way, turns the other, and swishes a rising shot which clips the outside of the near angle. Share

4m ago 15.40 EDT GOAL! Lille 2-1 Real Betis (Alexsandro Ribeiro 36) Perrin’s outswinging corner is a goodun and Alexsandro meets it well, leaping high to loop a header back the way the ball came. Share

5m ago 15.38 EDT Talking of West Ham, they’re drawing 2-2 at Bolton after just 38 minutes while, in our League Cup matches, Leyton Orient took the lead against Bradford but were quickly hauled back, and that match is 1-1 at half-time. Share

7m ago 15.37 EDT GOAL! Lille 1-1 Real Betis (Bartra 33) A short corner doesn’t work but the ball then goes back out to Fornals, of West Ham fame, whose cross is teased in towards the penalty spot, where Bartra meets it on the run, planting a fine header into the net. View image in fullscreen Real Betis' Marc Bartra is pleased to put the visitors back on level terms. Photograph: Jean-François Badias/AP Share Updated at 15.42 EDT

9m ago 15.35 EDT Greece, by the way, might just have a golden generation on their hands. Generally speaking, this means high expectations and no success, but don’t be surprised if they’re a factor at the Euros. Share

10m ago 15.34 EDT Giannis Konstantelias, Dortmund’s other Greek player, is already sidelined for some time with an ACL tear; let’s hope Karetsas isn’t badly hurt. Share

11m ago 15.32 EDT Rank news for Dortmund, who lose Karetsas to a non-contact injury. It didn’t look serious, but it didn’t look great either, and he’s replaced by Ethan Nwaneri. Share

12m ago 15.31 EDT Inter give the ball away and Vinicius streaks away, sliding into the middle where Diaz touches off for Mbappe .. but before he can control, Bisseck slides in to pretty much everything you can without giving away a penalty. I’d like to see it again, but I’m not certain he got the ball. Share

14m ago 15.30 EDT John Toshack once said that 90 minutes in the Bernabeu is a long time. Inter may be about to find out what he meant. Share

14m ago 15.29 EDT GOAL! Real Madrid 2-0 Inter (Valverde 23) Goodness me, what a mess. Josep Martinez in the Inter goal takes a pass from Pavard and decides away from home in the Bernabeu is where to show off his crafty drag-back. So he does, so Fede Valverde slides in, mugging him while he’s mugging himself off, and that is near enough curtains – after 23 minutes in which Inter have been the better side. View image in fullscreen Federico Valverde capitalises on Josep Martinez’s mistake and prods the ball into the Inter goal to double Real Madrid’s lead. Photograph: Jose Breton/NurPhoto/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Valverde celebrates with fellow goalscorer Kylian Mbappe. Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Uefa/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.41 EDT

17m ago 15.26 EDT Also missing from Madrid’s midfield: a controller. I don’t know, the game changes, of course, but the team which won multiple Big Earses had both Toni Kroos and Luka Modric. Share

18m ago 15.25 EDT Vini is sent bouncing through the middle but Pavard times his challenge beautifully, sliding in to avert the danger. Share

19m ago 15.24 EDT Email! “Let’s all hope that Inter win in controversial fashion just for the post-match quotes,” says Michael Meagher. “From last Friday: ‘The Betis players are more streetwise than the Madrid players, who are very honest.’ Don’t ever change José!” The Madrid players are also kind to small animals and fond of jigsaw puzzles. Share

21m ago 15.23 EDT GOAL! Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough (Strand Larsen 37) Palace badly need a win, any win, so will be glad to be ahead. View image in fullscreen Jorgen Strand Larsen of Crystal Palace places the ball past Boro keeper Sol Brynn to give the Eagles the lead. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Strand Larsen and the Palace fans celebrate. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at 15.37 EDT

22m ago 15.22 EDT Diaz is late on Martinez, lunging only to find he[s been chopped; free-kick Inter, on the edge of the box, and Calhanoglu will fancy this. He drills past the wall on its inside, but straight at Courtois, who again prangs to safety. Share

23m ago 15.20 EDT GOAL! Real Madrid 1-0 Inter (Mbappe 14) Caurtis jones looks to carry out of pressure but turns into trouble, poking to Bisseck and putting him under immediate pressure. His touch is really poor, Diaz prods forward, and Mbappe finishes with prejudice. Inter have started well, but they’re behind. View image in fullscreen Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe scores their first goal. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters View image in fullscreen Mbappe celebrates. Photograph: Mateo Villalba/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.25 EDT

26m ago 15.18 EDT Madrid’s midfield doesn’t just lack balance, it lacks a controller, and Lautaro strides through it, ignoring the support to shoot low from 20 yards. Again, though, Courtois parries. Share

27m ago 15.16 EDT GOAL! Lille 1-0 Real Betis (Ueda 12) Lovely work from Mbappe down the right, who chops inside, sending his man skidding off to who knows where. before gently curling a cross to the back post where, from a few yards out, Ueda can’t miss. View image in fullscreen Ayase Ueda of Lille celebrates after opening the scoring against Real Betis. Photograph: Franco Arland/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.44 EDT

29m ago 15.14 EDT I’d love to know what part of Madrid’s talent ID department watched Konate at Liverpool and thought yeah, him. Maybe they thought he’s a coach away from making the most of his physical gifts, but at 27, I can’t see it. What am I missing? Share

31m ago 15.12 EDT Beier goes down the left for Daortmiund and opens body to pass a terrific low ball through the corridor. Guirassy launches himself at it, but his slide arrives just a little bit late. Share

32m ago 15.11 EDT I don’t think the Madrid midfield is balanced, a particular problem given the unreliability of the centre-backs behind it; I’m a little surprised Mourinho isn’t relying on Rudiger, whose power, aggression and experience might be useful and who considers his boss his “footballing father.” Share

34m ago 15.09 EDT In Dortmund, Villarreal’s Comesana teases a ball into the box, but Oluwaseyi can’t impart any purchase on to his header. Share

35m ago 15.08 EDT Inter have started well and Lautaro pokes the ball wide then, when it comes into the middle, a deflection sits it up for Thuram, who wallops it with his laces … but straight at Courtois, who parries behind. The corner comes to nowt. Share

37m ago 15.06 EDT It’s probably me, but I find it amusing that, on their website, Uefa have gone for B. Dortmund, like it’s someone’s name. My dad always felt hard done by not to be given a middle name; I hope they’re bearing up. Share

39m ago 15.04 EDT And off we go in Madrid. Share

41m ago 15.02 EDT A moment is taken to remember those who died in the awful floods in Nepal. Godspeed. Share

42m ago 15.01 EDT I guess the existing structure was pretty special, so it didn’t need much work beyond the modernisation, but even so, they clearly did an outrageously good job. Camp Nou, on the other hand, was just a concrete bowl with, in some parts of the ground, plastic sets dumped into stone; there’s a lot more work to do making that good. View image in fullscreen Fans arrive at the Bernabéu. Photograph: Denis Doyle/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The Real Madrid dressing room is pretty snazzy. Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Uefa/Getty Images View image in fullscreen As is the interior of the stadium. Photograph: Ángel Martínez/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.16 EDT

45m ago 14.58 EDT Our teams are out in our various grounds, thus a question: I’ve not yet been, but is the Bernabeu the best ground refurb we’ve seen? Share

47m ago 14.57 EDT Right, we’re back. Ryan Christie has given Bournemouth the lead against Lincoln. Share

53m ago 14.50 EDT My computer is playing up so, to ensure we’re not interrupted once our feature games get going, i’m going to restart; see you on the other side in a few. Share

1h ago 14.44 EDT Our Carabao Cup fixtures are: Bournemouth v Lincoln City Crystal Palace v Middlesbrough Leyton Orient v Bradford City Millwall v Newcastle United The first three kick-off at 7.45, so in a minute from now, the fourth at 8pm. Share Updated at 14.44 EDT

1h ago 14.41 EDT Villa have won 3-2 at Brugge, and looked pretty good in so doing. Nicolas Jackson played really well, and strikes me as an Unai Emery type of player: underrated but, if he can sort out his major flaw, that being shooting, he can grow into a really serious striker. Everything else is in place. Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa: Champions League – live Read more Share

1h ago 14.39 EDT So, where is the game? Once upon a time, what Madrid did was largely up to Madrid players, but under Mourinho, it ain’t going out like that. Against a back three, the space tends to be behind the wing-backs and down the sides of the outside centre-backs, so I’d expect to see Dumfries and Alexander-Arnold ganging up on Bastoni and dragging him away from the middle, while Cucurella and Vinicius do the same on the other side, freeing up space for Mbappe and whichever of Bellingham and Valverde are box-crashing. Inter, meanwhile, will want their wing-backs targeting the space Madrid’s full-backs vacate, with their two up front looking to take advantage of Konate and Huijsen’s respective impetuousness and inexperience. This could be a really fun game. Share

1h ago 14.33 EDT Inter, meanwhile, look solid. They’ve won three from three in Serie A, and will, I think, look to clutter the centre of the pitch. That’s another reason I’d like to have seen Diomande on from the start, but Mourinho has – unusually for him – done without a defensively-minded midfielder. I’m looking forward to seeing how Curtis Jones does, as I think he’s a good player who’ll thrive with regular selection and greater responsibility. And there’s no disputing the danger Inter offer up front; I don’t fancy either Madrid centre-back against Thuram and Martinez. Share

1h ago 14.28 EDT Our main focus here, though, will be on Madrid v Inter. Mourinho’s men lost at Betis last weekend, and are without the suspended Eduardo Camvinga, Bernardo Silva and Arda Guler. As such Trent Alexander-Arnold comes in on the right of the central three – a move I doubt Aurelien Tchouameni likes all that much. I can’t say I think Alexander-Arnold is much use in that position – as Gary Neville once noted, most right-backs are failed midfielders – but he’s capable of creating something from nothing. I guess I’d quite like to see Yan Diomande on the right, but i’m not surprised Mourinho wants the extra body in midfield that Brahim Diaz can become. Share Updated at 14.29 EDT

1h ago 14.15 EDT There’s a lot to dig into there, right? It’s always interesting when new managers take over established teams, because chances are they’ll see things differently from their predecessors. City, for example, are now playing 4-2-3-1, not 4-3-3, and it doesn’t seem like Enzo Maresca fancies Rayan Ait-Nouri. Otherwise, Ayyoub Bouaddi makes his first start – he’s alongside Enzo Fernandez in a double pivot which lacks a bit of p&p – and a front four of Samenyo, Cherki, Foden, Haaland looks not bad. Share

2h ago 14.06 EDT Let's have some teams... Borussia Dortmund (3-4-2-1): Kobel; Gadou, Anton, Svensson; Ryerson, Sabitzer, Veerman, Beier; Karetsas, Nmecha; Guirassy. Subs: Drewes, Meyer, Bellingham, Chukwuemeka, Nwaneri, Fabio Silva, Kaua Prates, Inacio, Albert, Reggiani. Villarreal (4-4-2): Gulácsi; Mouriño, Pau Navarro, Renato Veiga, Sergi Cardona; Buchanan, Gueye, Saliba, Comesaña; Oluwaseyi, Mikautadze. Subs: Luiz Junior, Ruben Gomez, Logan Costa, Freeman, Alassane, Gerard Moreno, Alberto Moleiro, Akhomach, Carlos Macia, Pepe, Ayoze Perez. ** Porto (4-3-3): Diogo Costa; Varela, Perez, Kiwior, Alberto Costa; Rosario, Martim Fernandes, Veiga; Gomes, Silva, Pepe. Subs: Claudio Ramos, Joao Costa, Hwang, Sainz, Gimenez, Souza, Fofana, Cunha, Silva, L.Gomes, Moura. Manchester City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi Gvardiol; Bouaddi, Fernandez; Semenyo, Cherki, Foden; Haaland. Subs: Bettinelli, Rulli, Anderson, Ndiaye, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis,Allan, Khusanov, McAidoo, Lewis. ** Real Madrid (4-3-3): Courtois; Dumfries, Konate, Huijsen, Cucurella; Alexander-Arnold, Valverde, Bellingham; Brahim Diaz, Mbappe, Vinicius Junior. Subs: Lunin, Sergio Mestre, Endrick, Tchouameni, Carreras, Carlos Espi, Rudiger, Diomande, Thiago Pitarch, Jorge Cestero, Mario Rivas. Inter (3-5-2-): Martinez; Pavard, Bisseck, Bastoni; Diouf, Barella, Hakan Calhanoglu, Jones, Carlos Augusto; Lautaro, Thuram. Sports.title: Porto v Manchester City: Champions League – live
Sports.content:
now 15.43 EDT 40 mins: Gvardiol carries it forward, finds Semenyo and keeps chugging into the area. Semenyo switches the ball wide right to Foden, but left-back Fernandes shepherds him off the ball. Share

2m ago 15.42 EDT 39 mins: The home fans are raising the volume, but their team are yet to really threaten City inside the final third. Share

3m ago 15.40 EDT 38 mins: Veiga knocks the ball past Guehi and then barrels straight into him, looking for a foul. The referee is unmoved. Share

4m ago 15.39 EDT 36 mins: Yellow card! Gvardiol is again ruffled by William Gomes and brings the winger down. There’s a spot of afters, both players pointing the finger, but Gvardiol is justifiably booked. Share

6m ago 15.37 EDT 34 mins: Bouaddi is fouled by Veiga to end an unconvincing foray forward from the hosts. Share

7m ago 15.37 EDT 32 mins: Diogo Costa has made five saves already, and is keeping Porto on terms. That City move was triggered by a lovely Bouaddi pass forward; he has looked very assured so far. Share

8m ago 15.35 EDT 30 mins: Another City chance! Not sure how the visitors didn’t score here, as Nunes’ low cross finds Haaland, whose shot finds Costa with the goal gaping. The rebound falls to Cherki, whose rasping effort is also repelled – and Semenyo then takes a heavy touch, much to his teammates’ chagrin. Share

12m ago 15.32 EDT 28 mins: Another half-chance for City as Foden aims for the far corner, but sees his low shot beaten away by Costa. Share

14m ago 15.30 EDT 27 mins: Porto are allowing Semenyo too much space on the left, and his whipped cross finds Haaland, who heads a tricky chance just over the bar. Share

16m ago 15.28 EDT 25 mins: Porto almost trip the City offside trap with a lofted ball towards Andre Silva, but he goes a fraction early and the flag is raised. Share

17m ago 15.27 EDT 24 mins: Another slow-burning City passing move is ended by a foul, this time from Haaland, who leans on his marker too heavily. Share

18m ago 15.26 EDT 23 mins: Nice work from Enzo Fernandez, taking the ball cleanly from winger Pepe as Porto threatened to break. Share

19m ago 15.25 EDT 21 mins: City are penalised for a foul at the corner. You’d have backed Haaland to score with that chance, but his header was a touch too central. Share

20m ago 15.23 EDT 20 mins: Chance! Erling Haaland makes his first contribution, meeting Foden’s cross and powering a header on goal that Costa turns behind. City corner … View image in fullscreen Manchester City's Erling Haaland heads at goal. Photograph: Pedro Nunes/Reuters Share Updated at 15.29 EDT

22m ago 15.21 EDT 18 mins: Bouaddi, who has looked pretty comfortable so far, chips a pass out to Semenyo, who lets the ball skid out of play. Share

24m ago 15.20 EDT 17 mins: Porto advance into the City half but Silva and Gomes mess up an attempted one-two on the edge of the area. Share

25m ago 15.18 EDT 15 mins: Semenyo cuts in from the left and curls an effort on goal, but it’s comfortable for Costa. Share

26m ago 15.17 EDT 14 mins: Veiga gets in down the left and goes for the near post; Donnarumma sticks a leg out to deflect it behind, but the flag is up anyway. Share

27m ago 15.16 EDT 13 mins: Foden looks to whip a low cross in from the right, but Fernandes gets a challenge in and the ball deflects back to Diogo Costa. Share

29m ago 15.14 EDT 11 mins: City enjoying a little more possession now, with Bouaddi and Foden threading some neat passes together. Share

31m ago 15.12 EDT 9 mins: Guehi carries the ball out of defence and City work it to Cherki, who is shrugged off the ball by Varela. No free-kick, but Porto pass up the chance to break away. Share

33m ago 15.10 EDT 7 mins: Porto’s front three are pressing high and causing City problems, with Gvardiol almost taken off the ball by William Gomes. Share

34m ago 15.09 EDT 6 mins: A tentative Manchester City move forward ends when Haaland pushes his marker down. Share

35m ago 15.09 EDT 4 mins: Porto are missing their key midfield man, Victor Froholdt, tonight. He was knocked unconscious in a grisly clash of heads during their game against Moreirense on Friday, and spent the night in hospital. He is recovering but understandably not available tonight. Share

38m ago 15.05 EDT 2 minutes: Porto bring the ball forward but right-back Alberto Costa is penalised for hauling Gvardiol down. It’s raining hard, and the pitch looks slippery. Share

40m ago 15.03 EDT Kick-off Here we go, then. Porto are in their usual blue and white stripes; City are wearing their black and gold, bee inspired away kit. Share

41m ago 15.03 EDT Before kick-off, a minute’s silence to pay tribute to the victims of the recent flash floods in Nepal, which is impeccably observed. Share

47m ago 14.56 EDT Five minutes until kick-off, and the Estádio do Dragão feels suitably cauldronesque. It feels like there could be goals in this one – you can quote me on that later. Share

1h ago 14.37 EDT Head to head: Porto have played Manchester City four times in Europe, and are yet to beat them. In the 2020-21 Champions League, City won 3-1 at home and drew 0-0 away in the group stage – before going on to lose the final to Chelsea in this very stadium. The two sides also met in the 2011-12 Europa League knockouts, with City winning 6-1 on aggregate, before getting bundled out by Sporting in the next round. Share

1h ago 14.26 EDT Maresca has apparently introduced music to training sessions – Gabby Logan pushes him on the genre, and he says: “house music – I like house music, you know, boom-boom-boom.” Italo-house, perchance? Share

2h ago 14.10 EDT Enzo Maresca chats to Amazon Prime before the match: “It’s a hard place to come, but we’re going to try our best … it’s the first game, it’s going to be a long run. We’ll see where we are in December and January.” He’s asked about the pressure of following Pep Guardiola, but brushes it off. “I’m trying to do what I did at Leicester, at Chelsea, it’s nothing different.” On summer signings, he adds: “We have quality players, that means service for Erling [Haaland], movement between the lines.” Share

2h ago 14.05 EDT Team news Porto (4-3-3): Diogo Costa (c); Alberto Costa, Perez, Kiwior, Fernandes; Rosario, Varela, Veiga; William, Andre Silva, Pepe.

Subs: Claudio Ramos, Joao Costa, Hwang, Sainz, Gimenez, Souza, Fofana, Silva, Moura, Teixeira, Cunha, Luis Gomes. Manchester City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias (c), Guehi, Gvardiol; Bouaddi, Fernandez; Semenyo, Cherki, Foden; Haaland.

Subs: Bettinelli, Rulli, Anderson, Kovacic, Ndiaye, Ait Nouri, Vitor Reis, Allan, Khusanov, McAidoo, Lewis. Referee: Szymon Marciniak (Poland) Share

Sports.title: First-half treble powers Aston Villa to Champions League win at Club Brugge
Sports.content:
Aston Villa were 3-1 up after 43 minutes but were made to sweat for their first win of the season, emerging victorious from an entertaining Champions League opener against Club Brugge. John McGinn, who struck the only goal when Villa belatedly got their season up and running last September against Bologna, opened the scoring before goals from Emi Buendía and a first for Nicolas Jackson appeared to put Villa out of sight at half-time.

The Belgian side have become familiar foes since Villa returned to the big time, the glitziest club competition of them all; a freakish Tyrone Mings handball gifted the hosts a penalty, and subsequently victory, in 2024-25 and this time Aaron Wan-Bissaka conceded a second-half penalty to plunge a seesawing contest back into the balance. Villa had to live dangerously but equally could have won by a bigger margin.

Unai Emery had been at pains to radiate positivity despite another slow start – Villa picked up their first point of the Premier League season at the weekend and these goals represented their first of the campaign – but he was typically animated on the touchline here. He was particularly agitated midway through the second half when he felt, not for the first time this season, his substitutes were not ready for action. This time the culprits were Alysson, Ross Barkley and Lamare Bogarde.

Pau Torres was the unlikely catalyst for two of Villa’s three first half goals. McGinn’s opener was a product of the tall, softly-spoken Spanish centre-back roaming unchallenged to the edge of the box. Presumably it crossed Torres’s mind to shoot, though just as he was getting giddy, he spread play to McGinn, who guided a superb first-time, left-foot strike into the far corner of Yann Sommer’s goal. In starting here, the Switzerland goalkeeper became just the second goalkeeper to represent five clubs in the Champions League but it was a night to forget for the 37-year-old.

Club Brugge replied when Jan Virgili faced up Wan-Bissaka, this his full Villa debut, and located Hugo Vetlesen in the box, the Norway midfielder sending a crisp first-time finish beyond Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. The hosts were level for less than three minutes, a slick Villa move culminating in Buendía wheeling away in celebration. Jackson’s deft backheel supplied the tigerish João Gomes, who twisted inside the box and then passed the ball on to Buendía to do the rest.

View image in fullscreen John McGinn punches the air after giving Aston Villa an 11th-minute lead. Photograph: PA Wire/PA

Villa’s third arrived a few minutes before the half-time interval. Emery punched the air, his delight at establishing a two-goal advantage plain. Torres collected the ball on the edge of the Villa 18-yard box and after a couple of touches to shift the ball out of his feet, he sent a lofted pass spinning into the opposition half, where Jackson got in between the opposition centre-backs, Lee Han-beom and Brandon Mechele. Enter Sommer, who raced about 40 yards from goal. Jackson swiped the ball clear of the goalkeeper and then was too strong for Lee before passing into an empty net.

Things appeared rosy but Villa had to withstand heavy pressure after a video assistant referee review led the Swiss referee Sandro Schärer to penalise Wan-Bissaka for handball in the box. Nicolò Tresoldi sent Suzuki the wrong way from the penalty spot and a few minutes later the forward triggered a fine right-hand save from Suzuki, who pushed his shot on to the post. Victor Lindelöf tested the nerves of Emery, slicing a routine clearance when attempting to relieve the pressure. Villa, too, had chances, Jackson getting a shot away after latching on to a McGinn pass and Bogarde saw a shot cleared off the line by the Brugge full-back Joaquin Seys.

Sports.title: Air traffic chaos delays Arsenal flight to Naples for Champions League
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s preparations for their opening Champions League game against Napoli have been disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos that affected airports across the United Kingdom.

Mikel Arteta was forced to cancel his pre-match press conference at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Tuesday after Arsenal’s flight was severely delayed by an air-traffic control issue. The Arsenal manager and his players are understood to have remained at the club’s training ground in Hertfordshire as they waited for the delay to pass after completing their morning session as usual.

Club sources have insisted there has been no alteration to their planned schedule other than arriving later than expected to the team hotel. Uefa has also agreed to allow Arsenal to cancel their mandatory press conference due to the delays, which have also affected supporters travelling to Italy for the match.

Jurriën Timber is set to be part of the Arsenal squad for the first time since the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on 30 May after recovering from a groin injury. The Netherlands defender missed the World Cup due to the problem that has dogged him since March but Arteta said before Sunday’s win over Chelsea that Timber was close to returning.

Cristhian Mosquera is still absent with a muscle issue but Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who signed his first professional deal last month, is also part of the 23-man squad.

Napoli finished as runners up behind Inter in Serie A last season but have made a poor start this season under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. Kevin De Bruyne is expected to feature against Arsenal but they are without Scott McTominay, who had a successful surgical procedure to treat an irregular heartbeat yesterday. The 29-year-old is expected to resume training in two weeks.

Napoli are also are likely to be without influential former Fulham midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa as Allegri takes charge of his first Champions League match for four years. “People in this town have passion for the team, we have to start winning games again,” Allegri said. “We know we are challenging a very strong team – Arteta has done extraordinary things. Let’s face it with pride and desire.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Forget the hype machine – it’s the minnows who offer European interest
Sports.content:
CAN’T TOUCH THIS?

♫ ♪ 🎵 🎶 The champions ♫ ♪ 🎵 🎶! Bigger Cup is back, baby! Red-hot action from the world’s premier club competition across Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. Bigger Vase and Tin Pot clubs must wait for their slice of European action until after an international break almost as long as the Geopolitics World Cup itself. Rather like Gianni Infantino’s North American investment roadshow, Bigger Cup, with its revolving Swiss system, 36 teams reduced to 24 following 114 matches, has become baggier than MC Hammer’s trousers [now there’s a reference for the young readers – Football Daily Ed]. Back in Clive Tyldesley’s ITV pomp, ties such as Liverpool v Atlético, Napoli v Arsenal, and Real Madrid v Inter moved the dial, filling boozers and column inches.

Now, paywalled away and despite the whir of Darren Fletcher and Ally McCoist’s unrelenting hype machine, these nights can feel more routine, a golden goose not so much terminated as gathering dust on the mantelpiece. A trinket retaining monetary value but not as cherished as it once was. That holders PSG are so minted they can afford to play separate teams across Ligue 1 and Bigger Cup says much about modern football, where clubs and competitions have become content providers feeding an attention economy. In this case, that attention will run a deficit until, just like the GWC, the juice is in the knockout stages. There are, though, different dimensions to take solace in.

Uefa suits would argue, for all the ennui surrounding Manchester City facing Real Madrid 14 times since 2012 – they don’t meet in this year’s group – Bigger Cup offers pluralism in the presence of minnows and newcomers. Think of them like plucky non-league clubs in the FA Cup third round. There’s Serie A arrivistes Como, a cracking away trip for fans, with Cesc Fàbregas as well-regarded young coach, and Nico Paz as a potential successor to Lionel Messi. No pressure. Austria’s Lask, from Linz, will make their group stage debut, having sunk Celtic in the playoffs and featuring the talents of former Mangotsfield, Wealdstone, Yeovil, Chesterfield, Swindon and St Mirren defender Miguel Freckleton.

Azerbaijani football has previously been represented by Qarabag but Sabah are the new Azeri force, from a small municipality on the banks of the Masazir, an actual salt lake. Their coach, Valdas Dambrauskas, will be reunited with Manchester United. Using the funds from a small, Who Wants To Be A Millionaire win on Lithuanian TV in 2002, having phoned a friend, gone 50-50 and asked the audience, he emigrated to England, eventually becoming a coach at United’s soccer schools in 2004, beginning his long personal journey back to Old Trafford. Then there’s Slovan Bratislava, coached by a 2009 Big Cup winner in Yaya Touré, who succeeded Vladimir Weiss in the summer. Touré becomes the first African coach to lead a team in the competition’s group stage, ending a wait that has lasted far too long. Throw in the return of Bodø/Glimt and questions of whether the club from the Arctic Circle can keep on doing interesting things and not everybody has to be a billionaire’s plaything, though come the spring, it will certainly help.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Rob Smyth fromn 5.45pm BST for hot Bigger Cup coverage of Club Brugge 1-2 Aston Villa, followed by Niall McVeigh keeping an eye on Porto 1-1 Manchester City, plus Daniel Harris on the rest of Tuesday’s action.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I can’t change it. The truth is that I really don’t care. I know how to analyse football, I know why [they have won Bigger Cup twice]. I don’t know everything about football but I know more than most” – Kylian Mbappé, there, not wanting to get bogged down in the details as to why PSG have been Europe’s best team in the two years since he left.

Sports.title: More than 100,000 people add names to complaint against Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
More than 100,000 people have added their names to a complaint against Gianni Infantino, alleging the Fifa president has “at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty” through his interactions with Donald Trump.

The Reboot Fifa campaign was launched before the World Cup with the aim of delivering “the biggest complaint Fifa has ever received” over the organisation’s alleged failings of governance. The campaign has since extended the scope of its accusations to include the reversal of the ban for Folarin Balogun at the tournament and the aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.

The complaint was submitted on Tuesday to Fifa’s ethics committee and in a supporting letter the organisers of Reboot Fifa, the advocacy group Fair Square, call on the committee to take action. An original complaint, submitted in December of last year, failed to receive a response from the committee but has gained the backing of the Norwegian football federation and 50 European parliamentarians.

“The fact that 100,000 individuals added their names to this call for accountability is clear evidence of mounting public concern,” the Fair Square letter said. “As the independent judicial body tasked with the critical task of upholding the ‘integrity and reputation of football’, the ethics committee must not only act, it must be seen to act with appropriate haste, transparency and rigour.”

The letter lists eight incidents that form the basis of the Reboot Fifa complaint, which Fair Square alleges “provide compelling evidence that the Fifa president has, at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty in his efforts to ingratiate himself with the US president.”

. The incidents include the Balogun affair – where Trump admitted he asked Fifa to review the US striker’s red card – and the FFE scandal. They also cite the awarding of the Fifa peace prize to Trump, Infantino’s involvement in Trump’s Board of Peace in the Middle East and the Fifa president’s promise to work with Trump to “make not only America great again but also the entire world”, an act Fair Square suggests shows a failure to remain politically neutral.

Fifa, when approached for comment, pointed to a statement first published a month ago. “It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president,” the statement said.

“Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.”

Fifa confirmed on Sunday that Infantino would be seeking re-election for a fourth and final term next year despite pressure from Uefa and criticism from within the Asian confederation and Concacaf (the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation). Uefa has called on Infantino to stand down and recently announced its intention to pursue criminal claims in the US over the FFE plans.

Sports.title: Harry Kane and Alessia Russo among nominees for this year’s Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice have been nominated for this year’s men’s Ballon d’Or with Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood nominated for the women’s award.

The 30 men’s and 30 women’s nominees were revealed by France Football magazine on Tuesday, with the winners to be announced at a ceremony in London on 26 October. Ousmane Dembélé, who won the men’s award last year, has been nominated again, as has his France teammate Kylian Mbappé, who made history when he overtook Lionel Messi for all-time World Cup goals (22) at this summer’s tournament.

In the women’s field, two-time winner Alexia Putellas, Ewa Pajor and Melchie Dumornay are among the favourites to succeed Aitana Bonmatí. Winner of the past three awards, Bonmatí did not make the cut after missing most of the season through injury. The Spaniard returned at the end of Barcelona’s quadruple-winning season that included another Champions League title.

Kane is odds-on to win the men’s award after a club-record 61 goals in 51 games for German double winners Bayern Munich last season. He also scored six times at the World Cup for England, a tournament where Bellingham and Rice shone as well, the latter also playing a key role in Arsenal ending a 22-year wait for the Premier League title.

Quick Guide Ballon d'Or nominees: the full list Show Men's award nominees Jude Bellingham, Pau Cubarsí, Marc Cucurella, Ousmane Dembélé, Luis Díaz, Bruno Fernandes, Gabriel, Erling Haaland, Achraf Hakimi, Harry Kane, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Lamine Yamal, Sadio Mané, Marquinhos, Lautaro Martínez, Kylian Mbappé, Nuno Mendes, Lionel Messi, João Neves, Michael Olise, Willian Pacho, Julián Quiñones, Declan Rice, Rodri, Fabián Ruiz, William Saliba, Ferran Torres, Dayot Upamecano, Vinícius Jr., Vitinha. Women's award nominees Selma Bacha, Barbra Banda, Klara Buhl, Esmee Brugts, Mariona Caldentey, Scarlett Camberos, Kerstin Casparij, Temwa Chawinga, Cata Coll, Melchie Dumornay, Caroline Graham Hansen, Alex Greenwood, Patri Guijarro, Pernille Harder, Yui Hasegawa, Rose Lavelle, Mapi León, Lorena, Melvine Malard, Manaka Matsukubo, Vivianne Miedema, Ewa Pajor, Claudia Pina, Alexia Putellas, Wendie Renard, Alessia Russo, Khadija Shaw, Momoko Tanikawa, Caroline Weir, Tessa Wullaert. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Lamine Yamal, who won La Liga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain, is second favourite to win the award, followed by his club and international teammate Rodri. Messi, who has a record eight Ballon d’Or awards, is on the shortlist after guiding Argentina to the World Cup final and winning Major League Soccer with Inter Miami.

Russo finished third in last year’s voting and enjoyed another successful individual campaign, scoring 24 goals in 40 club appearances. Greenwood, the Manchester City captain, lifted the Women’s Super League and FA Cup last season.

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister ‘very sad’ Liverpool did not offer him a new contract
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister has said he feels “very sad” after Liverpool declined to offer him a new contract and admitted he rejected the chance to leave this summer.

Mac Allister revealed unhappiness over his contract situation before Liverpool’s Champions League opener against Atlético Madrid on Wednesday. The Argentina midfielder has two years remaining on his deal and believes he is effectively playing for a new contract having been informed no extension is on the table. Mac Allister confirmed he had offers to leave – Real Madrid and Manchester City were among those linked – but chose to stay because Liverpool can accomplish “something special” this season under Andoni Iraola.

“There was a chance [to leave] of course, like everybody knows,” said the 27-year-old, clearly keen to get the matter off his chest. “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very sad. I think everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club, every single day in training. Of course I have good games and bad games, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts, which makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time it makes me sad that I didn’t get mine. Of course there is still time [to be offered a new contract]. Fans don’t need to worry because I will give 100% until my last day. We will see what happens. There was options to leave this summer. I think right now I’m in the right club.”

Liverpool signed Mac Allister for a cut-price £35m in June 2023 by activating a release clause in his Brighton contract, which meant he was on a lucrative salary from the moment he arrived at Anfield. He claimed a new deal from Liverpool “is going to depend on how I perform during these years,” although he will be approaching 30 by the time his existing contract expires.

Asked why he chose to stay at Anfield this summer, despite his obvious discontent, Mac Allister replied: “Because this is the right club, that’s why. I love being here, this is something special. I feel we can be successful, what I want is to win trophies, and I think we have the right players and the right mentality to do great things, but everyone had to be on the same page.”

Mac Allister’s negotiating position would not have been at its strongest this summer after a disappointing season under Arne Slot, although he enjoyed a fine World Cup with Argentina. Iraola suggested Liverpool’s decision on Mac Allister might not be final.

The head coach, who will take charge of his first Champions League game on Wednesday while Diego Simeone leads Atletico for the 129th time in the competition, said: “I don’t know how much my players earn. I know how to improve my players, to help them win games. The same with Alexis and everyone else. He is very experienced player who has achieved massive things but I hope he can develop as a player and if all goes well those problems will be solved.”

Sports.title: The summer signing giving Unai Emery an extra attacking dimension - and the new man he will be alarmed by: Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa
Sports.content:
The summer signing giving Unai Emery an extra attacking dimension - and the new man he will be alarmed by: Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A first win of the season, a first goal for Nicolas Jackson and the ideal start to Aston Villa's Champions League campaign – but we may not see the best of Unai Emery's men until after the international break at least.

Heading into this game, Villa had not scored since Brian Madjo's strike in the Super Cup defeat by Paris Saint-Germain nearly a month ago.

But they put that right here as John McGinn, Emi Buendia and Jackson all struck before half-time. Hugo Vetlessen equalised briefly for Club Brugge, who closed the gap in the second half thanks to Nicolo' Tresoldi's penalty.

Both sides missed chances in a chaotic match that would have made Emery desperately nervous. The Villa boss craves control and here Villa rarely had it.

Yet after losing six key players over the summer and making an unconvincing start to the Premier League, this may be the result Villa needed to get their season moving...

Suzuki finding top speed

First Emi Martinez, now Zion Suzuki. Aston Villa certainly love a goalkeeper with 'main character' energy and just like Martinez, Suzuki looks like he will draw the spotlight.

Aston Villa got their first win of the season, a first goal for Nicolas Jackson and the ideal start to the Champions League

Zion Suzuki's range of passing with either foot is remarkable and gives Villa an extra attacking dimension

Where Martinez made his name through his astounding saves and unsavoury antics, it is the kicking that sets Suzuki apart. The Japanese's range of passing with either foot is remarkable and gives Villa an extra attacking dimension.

The game was barely a minute old when Suzuki picked out Aaron Wan-Bissaka, who was on the right touchline halfway inside the Brugge half. Wan-Bissaka and McGinn combined to set up a chance for Buendia but the Argentine missed the target.

Suzuki's kicking will naturally push the opposition back, just as a batter will hit over the top in cricket in order to spread the field. It is great to watch.

There may be some teething problems at the other end, though, as Suzuki's shot-stopping and aerial ability is not quite as convincing. But the early signs are that the £30million have been spent well.

Defensive fragility

Pau Torres was the only member of last season's first choice back four who played here and Villa looked vulnerable, especially out wide.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 7.5; Wan-Bissaka 4.5 (Bogarde 68, 6), Lindelof 7, *TORRES 8*, Maatsen 5.5; J Gomes 6.5, Kamara 7.5 (Barkley 68, 6); McGinn 7, Buendia 7 (Alysson 68, 6), Hemmings 7; Jackson 6.5 (Abraham 81) Scorers: McGinn 11, Buendia 22, Jackson 44 Booked: Maatsen, McGinn, Gomes Manager: Unai Emery 6 Referee: Sandro Schaerer 6

Ezri Konsa, Matty Cash and Lucas Digne were ultra-reliable as Villa finished fourth and won the Europa League – but now Konsa is at Arsenal, Digne is at Paris Saint-Germain and Cash was left at home due to muscle discomfort.

Aaron Wan-Bissaka had a torrid time against Brugge's Spanish winger Jan Virgili and was brought off after 68 minutes. When Konsa was at Villa, he would slot in at right-back at times like these. Instead, Emery had to send on Lamare Bogarde – his fourth-choice central midfielder – to handle Virgili.

It usually takes time for new signings to find their rhythm under Emery. Morgan Rogers was the exception, but players like Digne, Youri Tielemans – now with Manchester United – and Buendia all had to work hard to earn his trust.

Still, Emery will have been a little alarmed by Wan-Bissaka's display. The former Manchester United man, on loan from West Ham, can expect plenty of time in the analysis room after this showing.

Unai Emery will have been a little alarmed by new signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka's display

Emi Buendia is living proof that no player is ever totally out of the picture under Emery at Villa

Never give up

Emi Buendia is living proof that no player is ever totally out of the picture under Emery at Villa.

The playmaker suffered a serious knee injury on the eve of the 2023-24 season and in the following campaign, he was loaned to Bayer Leverkusen in January.

In summer 2025, Buendia was so far out of the picture that he was even considered by Birmingham, who had just been promoted from League One.

But Buendia stayed, won back his place in the team and in May, he scored one of the goals of the season in the Europa League Final to help Villa lift their first major trophy since 1996.

He finished off an excellent move here to restore Villa's lead in the first half. The club have added significant attacking talent this summer, with Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye arriving for more than £100million combined and Alejandro Garnacho joining on loan. All of them will have a tough job to squeeze Buendia out of the team.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree one of the most lucrative sponsorship deals in Premier League history with Turkish Airlines paying Reds £60MILLION-A-YEAR to front their shirts from next season
Sports.content:
Liverpool agree one of the most lucrative sponsorship deals in Premier League history with Turkish Airlines paying Reds £60MILLION-A-YEAR to front their shirts from next season

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool have signed a £300million deal with Turkish Airlines, who will become their main sponsor from next year.

It represents the end of an era after 17 years with Standard Chartered, with the branding on the kits of the men’s, women’s and academy teams changing from the start of next season.

The deal is thought to be worth in excess of £60m a year and the club believe it is among the most lucrative front-of-shirt agreements in Premier League history, in line with Manchester United and Manchester City.

Turkish Airlines flies to more airports in the world than any of its competitors and will invest big money into the football club.

Liverpool famously won the Champions League in the country in 2005, coming from 3-0 down to beat AC Milan on penalties in what became known as 'the Miracle of Istanbul'.

Chief commercial officer Ben Latty said: 'This is a milestone announcement for us and we are delighted to welcome Turkish Airlines as our main club partner from June 2027.

The new deal with Turkish Airlines brings to an end a 17-year deal with Standard Chartered

'The front of the Liverpool shirt holds a special place in the history of our club. Turkish Airlines is a globally recognised organisation with an extensive international network, and we look forward to beginning our partnership and building a strong relationship together, with already strong foundations built from those special memories back in 2005.'

Their most recent deal with Standard Chartered was understood to have been worth around £50m a year, making this a significant upgrade.

Liverpool believe one of their shirts is sold every 20 seconds around the world and they have more standalone retail stores than any club – they have recently just opened a branch on London's Oxford Street.

Standard Chartered will remain as a global partner when Turkish Airlines becomes the club's principal partner.

It will be just the third new sponsor in 35 years after Carlsberg were on the front of shirts from 1992-2010.

Sports.title: Arsenal caught up in UK airport travel chaos: Gunners forced to cancel Mikel Arteta's Champions League press conference in Naples with flights grounded by air traffic control 'technical failure'
Sports.content:
Arsenal's preparations for their Champions League tie against Napoli were disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos engulfing UK airports. The Gunners are back in European action on Wednesday when they face the Italian side in Naples. However, Mikel Arteta's pre-match press conference on Tuesday night had to be cancelled after Arsenal's flight to Italy was delayed. That was because of the air traffic control issues in the UK, with planes at most major UK airports grounded on Tuesday following a 'technical failure'. The problem has seen almost 300 flights from the UK cancelled, impacting thousands of holidaymakers along with the Premier League champions. Arsenal's squad are now not set to arrive in Naples until 9.30PM local time. Arsenal's preparations for their Champions League tie against Napoli were disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos engulfing UK airports Hundreds of flights were cancelled after an air traffic control 'technical failure' It was reported that they remained at the club's London Colney-based training ground while they were waiting for the issue to be resolved, before travelling to the airport later on when their new flight time was announced. At around 6.30PM, Arsenal then shared a video on their X account of the squad boarding a plane. In an update on Tuesday afternoon, National Air Traffic Services (NATS) said it had identified an issue with its 'flight processing system', adding that 'recovery will take some time', but said it had 'implemented a fix'. The organisation, which provides air traffic control services to 15 UK airports, gave no details as to the cause of the problem. But a spokesperson told the Daily Mail there is currently no indication the issue is due to a hack or other cyber incident. In more positive news for the Gunners, Jurrien Timber is set to be included in their squad for the match. The Dutch defender last featured off the bench in the Champions League final against PSG in May. However, that was his first appearance in more than two months and he subsequently missed the World Cup through injury. Speaking ahead of their Premier League tie against Chelsea on Sunday, Arteta had provided a positive update on Timber and hinted that a return was not too far away. 'Jurrien is in really good condition at the moment, he’s been a few weeks on the pitch and has been training with us, so he’s in a really good place,' Arteta said. 'We will decide [on his involvement on Sunday] after training [on Saturday].' Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber is set to be in their squad following a lengthy injury lay-off Napoli have three points from three league games so far this season and their squad includes former Premier League stars such as Kevin De Bruyne, Rasmus Hojlund and Billy Gilmour. Former Man United man Scott McTominay will miss out though, after recently undergoing corrective heart surgery. In a statement released earlier this month, Napoli had said: 'Following the onset of a mild benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay will undergo corrective surgery using a cardiac arrhythmia ablation (PFA) in the coming days. 'He will be available again after the international break.'
