Sports.title: Revealed: The little-known reason Jamie Vardy is forced to wait for Burnley debut after his surprise return to English football at 39
Sports.content:
Revealed: The little-known reason Jamie Vardy is forced to wait for Burnley debut after his surprise return to English football at 39

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jamie Vardy has been forced to wait for his Burnley debut due to a suspension hanging over from his time in Italy.

Vardy, 39, joined the Clarets on Sunday after leaving Cremonese at the end of last season following their relegation to Serie B.

Many expected Vardy to be involved in Burnley's game at Wrexham on Tuesday, yet his name was absent when the teams were announced.

And, Daily Mail Sport can reveal that Vardy's omission is due to the fact that he has to serve a one-match suspension after he accumulated five yellow cards in Serie A.

In Italy, a ban is automatically triggered after five cautions across the campaign, with Vardy picking up his fifth booking in Cremonese's final game of the season against Como.

Those rules differ to the Championship, with five bookings only leading to a ban if they come before the first 19 league matches.

Jamie Vardy must wait for his Burnley debut due to a suspension from his spell in Italy

Vardy picked up five yellow cards while at Cremonese, triggering a one-match suspension

The threshold is then increased to 10 yellow cards triggering a two-match suspension if they take place up to and including a team's 37th league game, with a three-match ban handed out for 15 yellow cards over the season.

Vardy was still present in Wrexham to cheer on his new team-mates, which include former England and Man City star Kyle Walker.

His absence is a blow to Nicky Hayen's struggling side though, with the Clarets currently bottom of the Championship after taking just two points from their first five league games.

Once his suspension is served, Vardy is expected to be Burnley's No 1 striker after they sold Zian Flemming to Ipswich on deadline day.

His deal has an option for a further year if the club are promoted, and it is understood he turned down offers from the MLS, Serie A and the Premier League to move to Turf Moor.

Speaking after his arrival was confirmed - which followed a summer of speculation about where he would end up - the veteran striker expressed his desire to propel his new team up the table.

Vardy told the club's website: 'I'm really happy to now be here at Burnley. This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town.

'I can't wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.'

Burnley boss Hayen also outlined his excitement about what his new striker will add to his struggling squad.

He said: 'We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley. His experience and leadership will be invaluable, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign. Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt.'

The move sees Vardy and his wife Rebekah return to England after he played in Italy for a year

Vardy, who moved to Italy with his wife Rebekah and their family last season, scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 appearances in Serie A for Cremonese.

The 39-year-old previously scored 200 goals in 500 matches for Leicester and won both the Premier League and FA Cup with the club. He is regarded as one of the Foxes' greatest ever players.

The striker, who had a Netflix documentary about his career released in May, also scored seven goals in 26 appearances for England and was part of the Three Lions squad for Euro 2016 and the 2018 World Cup.

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Stewards charged over derby assault axed by Old Trafford security, outrage at club's cup tickets warning, new stadium clears next hurdle and injury boost for Amad Diallo
Sports.content:
Five stewards charged with the assault of a Manchester United fan at the Old Trafford derby have been axed by the security firm used by the club.

Daily Mail Sport revealed two months ago that the men are due to appear at Manchester Magistrates’ Court in January, accused of attacking the 49-year-old supporter in the East Stand during a peaceful protest following United’s goalless draw with Manchester City in April 2025.

None of the five stewards are employed by United. They are understood to have been supplied to Controlled Solutions Group, the security company contracted by the club on matchdays, by HR Security and Protection Services.

A spokesperson for CSG told Confidential that the men will not be on duty at Old Trafford again. He said: ‘The five staff that were supplied to CSG by HR Security and Protection Services are no longer allowed to work on any CSG operations.’

The protest was in response to ticket price rises, and there will be more demonstrations when United face City at Old Trafford on Sunday. That's in response to the club’s controversial clampdown on ticket touts, which has led to United being accused of targeting innocent fans without proper evidence.

It was the subject of debate for more than an hour at the latest fans’ forum at Old Trafford in July, according to the minutes of the meeting which have now been released.

Five men will appear in court in January charged with an assault of a 49-year-old man during a post-match protest after the Manchester derby in April 2025

They reveal that supporters’ representatives ‘highlighted fans’ frustrations, anger and confusion with the communications between club and fans, with particular reference to the first wave of communications which were aggressive in tone, vague and anxiety provoking’.

United were also ‘asked whether the club recognised the growing perception among sections of the fanbase that long-standing season-ticket holders are being pushed out in favour of higher-yield hospitality and premium customers, and requested assurance that the purpose of the investigation was not to reduce the number of season ticket holders or facilitate a shift towards hospitality sales’.

United denied this was the case and chief executive Omar Berrada said: ‘There are no hidden intentions, the club is not trying to make financial gains from this process nor trying to reduce the number of season tickets available.

‘We acknowledge there are learnings to be made from this investigation, and the initial communications should have been better to explain to fans what we are trying to do, and we will improve on this as a club. The relationship with our fans is fundamental and we want to protect them and the club.’

Sabah a hard sell

It may have been more than two years since United played in the Champions League but that has not been enough of a carrot for supporters as tickets for Thursday's Sabah clash made their way to general sale.

United have thousands of registered members and yet with the game fast approaching, tickets are available as they look to pack out Old Trafford for a match which some supporters feel has the allure of a Europa League or Conference League fixture, against a team who were only founded nine years ago.

What the Sabah game has done is put those who opted into the cup scheme at the start of the season in a bind.

Fans were outraged on Monday night when a social media post went viral of a text message from Manchester United which read: ‘You don’t have a ticket for the Sabah game on Thursday – please do not come to Old Trafford. Tickets are still available to purchase here. If you don’t purchase a ticket, your season ticket will be deactivated for a future Premier League game and it may impact your away eligibility.’

United sources insist this is clearly marked out in the terms and conditions of any season ticket purchase and has long been the protocol for those who opt-in to cup competitions. They say the email was only sent to fans who had opted in but hadn’t paid for their ticket and didn’t respond to several emails – although the wording could have been better, which will be amended in future.

They also expect Old Trafford to be full for the Sabah game. But with the underdogs from Azerbaijan next up and Brighton at home in the Carabao Cup next week, it’s proving a very difficult sell.

Azerbaijani champions Sabah have qualified for the Champions League this season just nine years after being formed

Fosters? Good call

Foster + Partners have officially been appointed as the architects for United’s new £2billion stadium project.

Lord Foster, a close friend of United’s minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, has been at the forefront of plans to build the Ineos billionaire’s 100,000-seater ‘Wembley of the North’. Sources have confirmed the appointment of Foster + Partners after the club gave an update to the fans’ forum, saying ‘the focus now shifts to the design phase of the new stadium in partnership with Foster + Partners’.

United were asked at a previous forum meeting why an open tender was not held for the rebuild of Old Trafford, in keeping with the club’s fiduciary duty to its shareholders, after the controversial ‘tent’ design was unveiled at Foster + Partners headquarters in March last year.

United replied then that ‘a formal process to appoint a stadium architect is underway and will be made following appropriate due diligence and in line with our governance policies’. That process is now complete and not surprisingly Foster + Partners have emerged as the club’s choice.

Foster + Partners have been named as the architects of United's new stadium project

The firm released the first illustrations of what the new 100,000-seat 'Wembley of the North' could look like

Amad’s waiting game

Amad Diallo has yet to resume training on the grass at Carrington and is not expected to return to action until after the international break – although Confidential understands the United winger has an outside chance of being fit for the trip to Fulham a week on Sunday.

Diallo was injured in training before United’s opening game of the season at Hull City, and did not feature in the last two matches against Ipswich and Everton.

In addition, Marcus Rashford was taken off at Everton as a precaution after he was spotted holding his hamstring, and Michael Carrick revealed that the player ‘was feeling a bit of something’.

Meanwhile, United are being patient with Matthijs de Ligt’s return from back surgery so as not to put any pressure on the Netherlands centre back.

De Ligt is back in training but hasn’t played since the end of November, with United reluctant to put a timeline on his comeback.

Amad Diallo has an outside chance of being fit for the trip to Fulham a week on Sunday

Kids copy Carrick tactics

Under Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, the decision was taken that youth teams did not need to play in the same game model as the first team. It meant that players were not as adept at making the step up, either in first-team training sessions or in attempts to break into the senior squad.

But this season the Under 21s have reverted from their standard 4-3-3 into a more recognisable 4-2-3-1 with a false nine up top, rather than a conventional striker.

Where Matheus Cunha has led the line for Carrick’s first team, Under 21s boss Adam Lawrence has leaned on Amir Ibragimov to play a similar role, with rising star JJ Gabriel taking on Bruno Fernandes’ No10 position. Carrick and Steve Holland have continued to attend Under 21s and 18s matches this season.

It raises the question, with Chido Obi out on loan and Louie Bradbury having left permanently for Stoke weeks after signing a pro deal, of whether or not the long-term plan includes an orthodox No9.

Lawrence lands Youth League role

Confidential understands Lawrence is set to take charge of United’s Under 19s on their return to the UEFA Youth League.

He oversaw United’s last Youth League campaign in 2024 and after internal discussions as to whether he or Under 18s boss Darren Fletcher would manage the Under 19s, the job has landed at Lawrence’s door.

Talent isn’t in short supply with Tynan Thompson, Cristian Orozco, Gabriel and Ibragimov all still inside the age limit, which requires players to be born after January 1, 2008.

Bendito Mantato and Godwill Kukonki, mainstays around Under 21s squads, are also available to Lawrence, while it’s worth keeping an eye on Yuel Helafu, Noah Ajayi, Jayden Ngwashi and Jay McEvoy. Both Kai Rooney and Jacey Carrick feel like potential wildcards as part of a strong Under 18s side.

United host Sabah at Leigh Sports Village at 2pm on Thursday, six hours before the respective first teams lock horns at Old Trafford.

Adam Lawrence is set to take charge of United’s Under 19s on their return to the UEFA Youth League

Jaume’s a star pupil

Teenage midfielder Jaume Camacho Sidos has shown that he is one of United’s brightest young prospects on and off the pitch.

As well as shining for the club’s Under 18s, the 16-year-old has just passed all nine of his GCSEs with a perfect set of grade nines – equivalent to (if not better than) the old A*. Last year, Camacho Sidos was filmed speaking to Sir Alex Ferguson on camera as part of the club’s Lifeblood documentary series, titled United at Heart.

United’s new scholars achieved a strong set of results, with 75 per cent of all grades between four and nine. The club’s other academic achievements saw 11 second-year scholars complete their sporting excellence professional apprenticeship.

Six of the Under 21s, meanwhile, are studying towards BA (Hons) degrees through the PFA's football and business management programme.

It underlines United’s commitment to the development of their young players. Academy education manager Ian Smithson said: ‘The results highlight the players’ dedication and commitment to their studies and work both on and off the pitch, but are also testament to the care, attention, and excellent level of support they’ve received from our education staff.’

Sports.title: The streets won't forget! Former Tottenham and QPR star Adel Taarabt retires at 37, bringing an end to colourful 20-year career after stint in the UAE
Sports.content:
Former Premier League cult hero Adel Taarabt has said football has given him 'amazing memories' as he announced his retirement at the age of 37. Taarabt represented nine clubs during his career and most recently represented Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates top flight. He represented three English clubs during his career, initially joining Tottenham as a teenager from French side Lens. He is best remembered for his time at QPR, who he represented more than any other clubs during his career, while he also had a loan spell with Fulham. 'I knew this day would come, the time has come to close this chapter,' Taarabt wrote on Instagram. 'Football has been such a big part of my life for so many years. It gave me amazing memories, let me meet incredible people and live moments I will never forget. The ultimate ‘streets won’t forget’ baller 💫🤩 Adel Taarabt calls time on an incredible career 🙌#EFL pic.twitter.com/0JUZ56pGtM — EFL (@EFL) September 8, 2026 QPR icon Adel Taarabt has announced his retirement from football at the age of 37 Taarabt was central to Neil Warnock's QPR side winning the Championship in 2011 'I just want to say thank you to every club I played for, every coach, every teammate, every member of staff and of course every supporter who showed me love along the way. 'To every club I had the honour to represent, from Lens to Sharjah, thank you for being part of my story. 'Representing Morocco will always have a special place in my heart. 'There were good moments, difficult moments, mistakes, great nights… everything. But that was my journey, and I wouldn’t change it. 'Alhamdulillah for everything.' Taarabt was known for his skillful dribbling ability, with the attacking midfielder catching the eye during his 15 appearances at Tottenham. He enjoyed a successful loan spell at QPR, which led to Taarabt signing permanently for the then Championship side. Taarabt was named Championship Player of the Season in 2011 after scoring 19 goals and providing 21 assists to help Neil Warnock's side earn promotion to the Premier League as champions. Despite being known for his skilful and unpredictable game, Taarabt surprisingly became a defensive midfielder during a spell with Portuguese giants Benfica He spent a further two seasons at the club, making 164 appearances in total in which he scored 34 times, before loan spells at Fulham and AC Milan. Taarabt left QPR on a permanent basis in 2015 to join Benfica and later Genoa on loan. He was notably frozen out of the first-team set up at Benfica but memorably regained a place in theside in an unexpected defensive midfield role having been known for his skill and unpredictable approach to the game. The latter stages of his career saw Taarabt join Al-Nasr and Sharjah in the UAE. Taarabt also represented Morocco 30 times, scoring four goals.

Sports.title: Inside Man City's summer of streamlining: Enzo Maresca's new strategy for squad depth, where Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez fit in and how Hugo Viana quickly fixed the mistakes of 2025
Sports.content:
Inside Man City's summer of streamlining: Enzo Maresca's new strategy for squad depth, where Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez fit in and how Hugo Viana quickly fixed the mistakes of 2025

Elliot Anderson had only been back in the country for 48 hours, still processing England's defeat by Argentina, when his day arrived. Going up to Manchester to officially sign the deal of a lifetime before enjoying deserved time off on two separate holidays with his brothers and girlfriend.

The interest had been heavily signposted, with Manchester City making relevant enquiries just before Christmas, and the 23-year-old was earmarked as the man to add much-needed punch into a midfield that felt light and yearned for the Rodri of old.

He had been anticipated to arrive, smiling with Hugo Viana and meeting Enzo Maresca, as the most expensive British footballer of all time - though that £116million fee paid to Nottingham Forest was eclipsed by Chelsea and Morgan Rogers within days of the agreement being reached during the World Cup.

And he didn't even end the transfer window as City's record signing either, Enzo Fernandez sourced from Chelsea for £125m in the nick of time on deadline day. So late – City threatened to pull out amid the posturing – that he was having a medical at almost 10pm and posing for photographs in complete darkness.

But irrespective of the finances and what ultimately transpired in City's hectic window, the conversation around the dinner table at the Ivy Asia on July 22 between Anderson, his family and representatives would have circled to how he was one of the faces of this rebuild. A pillar of Maresca's midfield, huge trust in somebody whose stock is rising rapidly yet will only taste the Champions League for the first time in Porto on Tuesday.

Midfield was clearly the area identified as the one requiring most surgery. Anderson's early displays, powerful and authoritative, suggest he is picking up from where he left off in taking more responsibility in an England shirt. Next to him stands the divisive character of Fernandez, a proven winner, a signing Maresca pushed for personally, and who offers a nastiness that City have probably missed in the past two years.

Elliot Anderson will be a pillar of Enzo Maresca's midfield - huge trust in somebody whose stock is rising rapidly yet will only taste the Champions League for the first time on Tuesday

Next to him stands the divisive Enzo Fernandez, a proven winner, a signing Maresca pushed for personally, and who offers a nastiness that City have probably missed in the past two years

Ironic, really, that City's new-look engine room is on show in Europe for the first time at the Estadio do Dragao – the scene of the 2021 final defeat by Chelsea, when Pep Guardiola went without a conventional holding midfielder. The decision is still debated in the bars of Manchester to this day.

When taking deep breaths at 11pm last Tuesday, City were satisfied with their work, totalling a net spend of £145m following heavy sales, and there is an insistence that the squad is now in a significantly more advantageous position than a year ago.

That is largely because the two windows of 2025 have aged poorly, with Tijjani Reijnders, Omar Marmoush and Nico Gonzalez all having been let go less than 18 months after landing.

City rectified those mistakes by earning their money back on all three, with Tottenham owning an obligation to purchase Marmoush for £60m once his loan finishes. And not forgetting the astonishing £85m for two-goal Savinho, bought a year earlier.

Another 2025 signing, Rayan Ait-Nouri, cannot buy a game at left back and Manchester United even asked whether the Algerian was available for transfer. In truth, allowing Ait-Nouri to leave as well would have left City too short and that throws up an intriguing subplot to their summer.

It feels deeper, this squad. It feels more complete. But there are fewer players. Twenty-two senior outfielders last year plays 20 this. In the Treble season, there were 18.

With ten first-teamers departing since May, six coming in, this has been a streamlining. Is the thinking clearer now than it was a year ago, when Txiki Begiristain was handing over and Guardiola's time began drawing to a close? The proof will be in the progression over the next three years and these past few months will likely define Viana's tenure at the Etihad.

The idea on the squad's make-up appears to have shifted slightly, with more emphasis placed upon individual players battling a team-mate in specific positions – much like how Thomas Tuchel ran the England team in the build-up to the World Cup – rather than demanding they are capable of performing in three or four different areas.

How that works or evolves will only become clear over time, as with much of this new era, and City's idea that Antoine Semenyo is the alternative No9 to Erling Haaland suggests they will still be leaning on some versatility.

Rayan Ait-Nouri cannot buy a game at left back and Manchester United even asked whether the Algerian was available for transfer

City's idea that Antoine Semenyo is the alternative No9 to Erling Haaland suggests they will still be leaning on some versatility

HAALAND FEARS MENTAL TOLL OF PLAYING AT WORLD CUP Erling Haaland has warned that a non-stop year could impact his season with Manchester City despite a flying start. The Norway international had three weeks off after his exploits at the World Cup but has claimed to be mental fatigued. Haaland has netted three Premier League goals from three starts, with manager Enzo Maresca mindful of over-playing the striker after featuring in more matches last season than in any other during his career. 'When I came back it was like "wow – it's good to be home" but it was weird because so much had happened and I hadn't digested it,' Haaland said. 'The new season started and I didn't even have a pre-season. I normally have a bit of pre-season but this time, just nothing. 'The physical side will come – if you manage to stay injury free. But you need to be sharp mentally as well – and that's not easy. 'We need to have that eager feeling to go back but we don't because there is no time to properly stay away from football because there are so many games and the season is longer.' Haaland added on his YouTube channel: 'I'm not complaining because it's still a positive thing that you get to play football throughout the whole year and live off it. 'I've never been in this situation before – I never played a World Cup so I don't know how it is.' Maresca will continue to monitor the stars who went into the final week of the World Cup, with Jeremy Doku having already suffered an injury on his return and unavailable for Tuesday's Champions League encounter at Porto. 'It's not easy for them,' Maresca said. 'I think it is correct in the moment that you see these kind of players that they start to be tired. It's correct to give them some rest. 'It can be one game out or one week away. It depends on which moment we are in. But the priority is to allow the players to be good and happy. In the moment you see them tired the risk is there. We need players at 100 per cent.' Jack Gaughan in Porto

What follows over the next ten days – Porto, United at Old Trafford on Sunday and then the Carabao Cup against Norwich City – should provide clues as to what sort of City manager Maresca sees himself as.

Settled side or heavy rotation? There will have to be some caution – Porto have won all six of their games this season, conceding only once, and Guardiola found out how troubling the Champions League league phase can be.

With the derby on the horizon, Maresca must decide whether to go same again or mix things up in Portugal. Given it certainly looks as if the quality gap between individuals fighting for the same position has narrowed with the recent business, there could be more confidence in tweaking with the sort of regularity that Guardiola was famed for.

Maresca has talked up the need for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye to be offered minutes, while Phil Foden didn't start against Coventry City.

Before they flew out to Porto on Monday afternoon, Maresca had the music blaring during the early part of City's training session, as is customary under him. The Italian is quietly convinced he will get a tune out of City's reimagined squad.

Sports.title: Why Borussia Dortmund stand is empty for Champions League as team fail to sell tickets
Sports.content:
Why Borussia Dortmund stand is empty for Champions League as team fail to sell tickets

Borussia Dortmund will face Villarreal in the Champions League but will potentially have one area of the stadium empty

View 2 Images Borussia Dortmund will host Villarreal in the Champions League at Signal Iduna Park (Image: Christof Koepsel/Getty Images)

Borussia Dortmund’s match against Villarreal in the Champions League will have a noticeably empty section in the stadium this week. Dortmund and Villarreal will go head-to-head in each of the club’s first European matches of the season, with the fixture taking place at Signal Iduna Park.

However, one section of the famous stadium will have zero supporters watching from the stands, with Villarreal not filling their full allocation for away supporters.

Champions League rules allow away teams to have 5% of the overall capacity of a stadium available for travelling fans.

Dortmund’s home stadium has an overall capacity of around 81,000, meaning that Villarreal would have been entitled to just over 4,000 of their fans to watch the match inside the famous venue.

However, a report in Sport Bild has claimed that Villarreal has informed Dortmund that they will not fill their full allocation for the fixture.

It has been claimed that the Spanish club have sold just 39 tickets for away fans to watch the game in Germany, and as a result, has been given back to Dortmund for home fans.

The report further claims that, after being informed of Villarreal’s ticket sale numbers, Dortmund have decided to accommodate those fans in the West Stand, instead of the North East corner, which is typically reserved for away supporters. That will leave an entire section of the ground empty.

Dortmund boss Niko Kovac was quick to emphasise the difficulty of the match ahead for his team as they prepare to face a Villarreal side that finished third in La Liga last season.

"They finished third last year and are playing in the Champions League for the second year in a row," Kovac told said, via Dortmund's club website.

"Normally, the top three spots in Spain are locked up. If you break into that group (alongside Barcelona, Real Madrid, and Atletico Madrid) that really says something!"

Kovac added: "They have a new coach now, but they continue to play the Spanish style with a lot of possession.

View 2 Images Borussia Dortmund manager Niko Kovac has spoke about the match with Villarreal (Image: Alexandre Simoes/Borussia Dortmund via Getty Images)

"We'll have to make sure we reduce their time in possession. When we have the ball, they can't play their game and have to defend more, which will hopefully work in our favour. It's going to be a very difficult game."

Eight players could miss Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid as Cody Gakpo absent from training

Liverpool will be without several key players when they take on Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday night, with injuries and squad decisions set to limit both sides

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo has emerged as an injury concern for Liverpool (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Sports.title: Value Scope Extra: Steve Jones' best bets for the St Leger Festival
Sports.content:
There's no lengths Sir Mark Prescott won’t go to in search of a decent winner.

Racing’s favourite baronet is well known for sending his horses to corners of the world to run at racecourses some trainers might not even knew existed.

Alpinista won top-level prizes at three different German tracks before giving Sir Mark his greatest day when landing the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe four years ago.

Last weekend, he sent another smart mare, Tiffany, across the Atlantic to secure Grade 2 glory at Kentucky Downs.

‌



She had won a Group 1 at Hoppegarten in Germany last month and her most recent success underlines the red-hot form of the Newmarket trainer’s team.

This week, Prescott is staying much closer to home, with Doncaster’s Betfred St Leger Festival demanding most of his attention. He heads to South Yorkshire having saddled nine winners from just 26 runners in the last couple of weeks.

Among his runners this week are Consent in the Park Hill Stakes (Thursday), May Hill Stakes hope Martinet (Thursday) and Sceptre Stakes possible Moon Target.

View 2 Images Sir Mark Prescott has a strong team heading to Doncaster this week

‌



Another Newmarket stable to follow over the next few days is that of John and Thady Gosden.

The father-and-son partnership have had 11 winners at the St Leger meeting from 44 runners since they teamed up five years ago. They have turned a level-stakes profit of more than 19pts in that time.

Those stats are very much in line with Gosden senior’s results at the classic festival when he was the sole name on the training licence.

In the 10 years before his eldest son officially joined him, he sent out 23 winners from 96 runners with a level-stakes profit of more than 11pts.

‌



The Gosdens will have a strong team at Doncaster. As well as numerous chances in the Group races, they have several potentially interesting runners in the handicaps, including Devil’s Peak (Thursday), Fifth Column (Saturday), Archer Royal (Sunday) and Valedictory (Sunday).

Archie Watson hasn’t got any Doncaster entries but he is a trainer definitely worth following.

He’s endured a tough summer but his team has turned the corner in some order. From the beginning of May until the end of August, he trained just 13 winners from more than 200 runners.

Already in September he has notched up three winners from 11 runners. Three of the beaten horses finished runner-up. He could have a fruitful weekend, especially at Lingfield.

Sports.title: Conor Benn sent brutal five-word warning ahead of Ryan Garcia grudge match
Sports.content:
Conor Benn sent brutal five-word warning ahead of Ryan Garcia grudge match

Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia will meet on Saturday night in a mouthwatering grudge match for the latter's WBC welterweight title in Las Vegas

View Image Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia ahead of their fight (Image: Fanatics)

Ryan Garcia is coming with 'mean intentions' and has vowed to KO Conor Benn in under five rounds.

‌



The two boxing stars will go head-to-head in Las Vegas on Saturday night - with Garcia putting his WBC welterweight title on the line. The 'Destroyer' will be looking to turn his dream of winning a title into reality - 34 years after his father Nigel Benn first won the coveted green belt after a vicious knockout of Mauro Galvano.

‌



But Benn faces a potential battle with the scales ahead of his first fight at 147lb in over four years. The 29-year-old year comes into the clash off the back of a points victory over Regis Prograis - which was contested at a catchweight of 150lb. Benn has not really had to worry too much about cutting weight prior to his clash with Prograis after competing at middleweight for his two epic encounters with Chris Eubank Jr last year.

‌



Despite having to boil himself down in order for his fight with Garcia to be made official, Benn is leaving no stone unturned in preparations for the world title bout. Welterweight champion Garcia welcomes the challenge, but will be in no mood to mess around as soon as the first bell sounds.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson did not stutter when offering Conor Benn vs Ryan Garcia prediction
Sports.content:
Mike Tyson did not stutter when offering Conor Benn vs Ryan Garcia prediction

Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia will meet in a WBC welterweight showdown this weekend, and boxing legend Mike Tyson was eager to offer his verdict on the clash

View Image Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia face off ahead of their fight (Image: Fanatics)

Mike Tyson has praised the work of Conor Benn, but is backing Ryan Garcia to win their grudge match on Saturday night.

‌



The pair will go head-to-head in Las Vegas in a 147lb showdown - with Garcia set to put his WBC welterweight title on the line. Garcia won the coveted green belt earlier this year after dominating Mario Barrios over 12 rounds in their Sin City dust-up.

‌



For Benn, he will be itching to emulate the success of his father Nigel - who famously won a WBC belt 34 years ago when he knocked out Mauro Galvano. Benn Sr would famously go on to defend the title nine times before dropping it to Thulani Malinga back in 1996.

‌



With many fans on the fence as to who will win Saturday night's mouthwatering bout, boxing icon Tyson believes there's a clear winner. When asked who will win, he told FightHype TV: “Ryan," before adding: “We’ll see [if Garcia can knock him out]. Conor’s getting better.”

Garcia has vowed to put on a show and hopes to stop his upcoming advesary in five rounds or less, telling ESPN: “I’m here to make a statement. I’ve not been shy about that. I’ve said five rounds and below. That means I’m coming with mean intentions and I’m not here to dance my way to a decision, but I’m also not here to be stupid, at the end of the day. But would it be amazing? Yes.”

‌



This weekend's fight marks Benn's first contest at welterweight in over four years. On that night, he needed just two rounds to stop Chris van Heerden in Manchester. He has since moved up as high as middleweight - for his two historic meetings with Chris Eubank Jr.

Last month, the 'Destroyer' revealed that he will not be continuing at 147lb after his fight with Garcia after expressing his desire to move back up in weight. “Yeah, it’s hard. It’s brutal," he told Ring Magazine when discussing weight cut ahead of his return. "This is my last fight at 147. When I win the world title, I’ll move on.

That said, he's solely focused on Garcia and is clearly leaving no stone unturned, saying: "I don’t care what he’s doing. Like it makes no difference. It doesn’t concern me at all. All I know is I’m working extremely hard to come out victorious. No doubt I’ll be looking for the stoppage myself. I think I’ll stop him. Yeah, I do.”

Sports.title: Man Utd fan group announce protest plans after club 'crossed the line' with ticket plans
Sports.content:
Man Utd fan group announce protest plans after club 'crossed the line' with ticket plans

Manchester United supporters are being urged to join a protest by a fan group, who remain frustrated by the way the club attempted to rid of certain individual's season tickets

View 2 Images Man Utd fans are eyeing a protest this Sunday as the club's hierarchy continue to come under fire

A Manchester United fan group wants to lead a unified protest against the club before this Sunday's Manchester derby after what they called a "season ticket ban fiasco".

‌



The Red Devils will play their neighbours City this weekend at Old Trafford in what is one of the biggest games of their season, but supporters are still furious by how the club handled plans to cut down on ticketing touts in the summer.

‌



United said in August that an independent company had "uncovered significant and organised touting," after taking a look at account activity and, as a result, lifelong fans were warned that they faced the threat of losing their tickets.

‌



The Premier League giants later accepted that their investigation had "caused significant concern and distress for some supporters" with some fans feeling as if they "being treated unfairly."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

That bad feeling has lingered and The 1958 group believe a "line has been crossed," and want to make that known to the club's bosses with a peaceful protest ahead of this weekend's game.

‌



A spokesperson for the fan group said: "Manchester United supporter groups are being called upon to all stand together following reports of bans and season ticket sanctions without clear and compelling evidence always being presented.

"For generations, match-going Reds have given their time, money and loyalty to Manchester United, home and away. That loyalty deserves to be treated with respect. This is not about one group or one individual. It is about how Manchester United treats its match-going supporters. It may not affect you today, it may not next time but that day is coming for all of us. All Reds. All groups. One voice. Show the evidence. Lift the bans."

View 2 Images Man Utd fans have held up banners already this season, referencing the events of the summer

‌



The 1958 wants any previous differences between supporter groups to be put aside and asked that fans gather outside the Bishop Blaize pub near Old Trafford at 3pm on Sunday - an hour and a half before kick-off.

The supporter group co-signed a statement released in July criticising the club's actions, where they expressed a culture from within the club that was "ban first and ask questions later".

A number of fan-affected decisions have seen the United hierarchy criticised. They previously removed concession prices for tickets and moved several fans to new spots inside the stadium to accommodate more premium hospitality seating.

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or 2026 nominees announced in full as Harry Kane discovers chances of glory
Sports.content:
The nominees for this year's Ballon d'Or have been revealed, with Harry Kane among those in the running for the prize.

The Bayern Munich and England striker has enjoyed another stellar season for both club and country and is one of the betting favourites ahead of the ceremony, which will take place in London next month.

Kane scored a staggering 73 goals last season, enjoying one of the best campaigns of his remarkable career - but it remains to be seen if that will be enough for him to become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane is joined the 30-man long-list by international team-mates Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice.

‌



Bruno Fernandes, the Manchester United captain, is also in the running for the award after breaking the Premier League assist record last season after creating 21 goals. Gabriel of Arsenal and Manchester City's Erling Haaland are among the other Premier League players included.

Lamine Yamal, Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappe are among the other notable contenders for the award.

View 2 Images Harry Kane is in the running for the Ballon d'Or award after a remarkable season for club and country (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal have been nominated for the Team of the Year award after winning the Premier League for the first time in 22 years, while their manager, Mikel Arteta, and Unai Emery are both up for the coach of the year prize.

There is more Arsenal representation in the goalkeeper of the year category, with David Raya up for the award.

Sports.title: Emma Wilson relishing home waters at windsurfing World Championships
Sports.content:
Emma Wilson relishing home waters at windsurfing World Championships

Defending world champion Emma Wilson enjoyed the opportunity to race on home waters as she got underway in Portland

View 2 Images Emma Wilson competes in the iQfoil Class at the 2026 iQFoiL Worlds Weymouth - Portland on the 07 September, 2026. (Image: @Sailing Energy)

Defending women’s windsurfing champion Emma Wilson is feeling positive after opening up her Musto iQFOiL World Championships 2026 account in Weymouth and Portland.

‌



Britain’s most successful female Olympic windsurfer took fifth place in the standings by the end of the first day of competition at the Weymouth and Portland National Sailing Academy, picking up a race win in her second heat.

‌



Wilson finished fifth in her other sprint slalom heat, before placing seventh and 16th in the longer course races, the latter result discarded from her record as her worst result, for a net points tally of 13. Wilson is joined by British Sailing Team compatriot Islay Watson in the top five.

‌



The three-time iQFOiL world medallist and two-time Olympic bronze medallist was happy after the opening day of racing.

“I’m really happy with the day, glad to get racing and feels like it’s been a big build-up,” Wilson said. “Once I was on the course, it just felt like racing again. It was super up and down with the rain.

"At the start we had sprint racing with the lighter winds and then the wind picked up for a longer course. It was not that windy though, the wind was pretty light and it was physical.

‌



View 2 Images Emma Wilson competes in the Qfoil Class at the 2026 iQFoiL Worlds Weymouth - Portland on 07 September, 2026. (Image: @Sailing Energy)

“I like everything and that’s probably why I don’t mind what we go out in. That’s strength of mind, to be good in every condition. I’m not really phased by the course they'll put up. I was nervous before the first race, so then once we got racing, I was next to my mates and I was like, ‘Oh this is normal,' it was good fun actually to race at home.

“I knew the level was going to be super high. We all know each other, and tomorrow I will just focus on myself again and try my best.”

Article continues below

The preliminary series will decide who enters the women's gold and silver fleets for the Saturday 12 September finale in Weymouth Harbour, with a Fan Zone taking place in Weymouth Pavilion. Wilson is in a strong position to make the gold fleet and give herself the chance to race for medals in Weymouth.

A further result will be discarded when eight races have been completed by Wilson, with the top 35 sailors expected to make the cut by tomorrow evening.

The Musto iQFOiL World Championships 2026 are taking place from 7-12 September. Get closer to the action on the final day by visiting the Fan Zone on Weymouth Pavilion to enjoy a full day of live racing, big-screen coverage, music, family activities, food and opportunities to get out on the water. Find out more at rya.org.uk

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
