World.title: Artist puts Kashmiri poet Lal Ded's mysticism on Pashmina
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: MF Husainâs horses meant power. Flat, bold, Cubist, built for scale like the Bollywood billboards he once painted in Mumbai. Masood Hussainâs horse is painted on Pashmina and dyed in the wool â carrying the earliest Kashmiri poetry, passed down orally for 600 years before anyone wrote it down.This is a sharp turn from familiar ground for Srinagar-based Hussain, whose work for years has chronicled Kashmirâs conflict, grief and everyday life. For the first time, he has painted Lal Vakhs â mystical four-line verses of 14th-century Kashmiri poet Lal Ded â on Pashmina shawls.Twenty shawls. Two years. âThese are painted shawls based on Lal Vakhs. I selected 20 Vakhs, then I conceived them and painted them,â Hussain said Monday at an exhibition in Srinagar.Lal Ded, also known as Lalleshwari, was born near Srinagar in a Kashmiri Pandit family. Abused at her marital home, she left at 26 to become an itinerant Shaiva mystic. Muslims called her Lal Arifa. Her Vakhs â from the Sanskrit vaak, meaning âspeechâ or âsayingâ â are among the earliest compositions in Kashmiri and a foundation of its literary tradition.Hussainâs shawls give those words a visual life. One features what Hussain calls a celestial horse â a rider moving beneath a sky stitched with constellations.Other shawls turn towards Lal Dedâs references to death, spiritual passage and the unseen.The idea took root after Hussainâs collaborations with Irish poet Gabriel Rosenstock, who died of cancer in April this year. Their first project marked Mahatma Gandhiâs 150th birth anniversary. Rosenstockâs 150 minimalist haikus and tankas were paired with Hussainâs watercolours, bringing Irish culture, Kashmiri artistry and Gandhian philosophy of peace into one book.âI mostly painted Kashmir and its conflict. Once I collaborated with Rosenstock, a lot changed,â Hussain said. âWhy not work on Kashmir Sufism, Rishi culture, syncretic culture and convert them into paintings? Why not start on Lal Ded on Pashmina? I got the idea.âLal Ded walked barefoot, wandered, spoke in riddles. Hussain began by reading extensively about her and her poetry. âA lot has been written, but no one has given it a visual shape. I tried,â Hussain said. The medium is the message. It is an old poetry in a new skin â mysticism that can be worn.

World.title: Ladakh's tourist footfall continues rising; August sees most foreign visitors
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Ladakh has recorded a sharp rise in tourist arrivals this year, with 4,05,085 visiting the Union Territory in the first eight months of 2026, exceeding the 3,35,872 tourists recorded for all of 2025.

âIn just eight months of 2026, the total tourist footfall has exceeded by 20.6% from the total tourist arrivals recorded in 2025,â a govt spokesperson said.

Aug 2026 saw the highest foreign tourist footfall recorded in any month so far this year, with 10,075 foreigners travelling to Ladakh. âThis is also considerably higher than the 8,148 foreign tourists recorded in Aug 2025,â the spokesperson said.

The growth was recorded across both domestic and foreign tourist segments.

âDuring the first eight months of 2026, Ladakh received 3,71,739 domestic tourists and 33,346 foreign tourists, compared to 2,44,308 domestic and 25,082 foreign tourists during the corresponding period in 2025,â the spokesperson said.

In Aug, major festivals like Changthang Nomadic Festival, the first-ever Black-necked Crane Festival, Suru Summer Festival, and Ladakh Book Festival added new attractions to Ladakhâs tourism calendar and attracted a huge number of tourists, the spokesperson said.





âThe first edition of Black-Necked Crane Festival alone saw the participation of more than 10,000 people from India and abroad. These festivals showcase Ladakh regionâs unique culture, nomadic traditions, wildlife and natural heritage,â he added.

Ladakhâs tourism calendar remains active in Sept as well, with a series of major events lined up, including Ladakh Bike Week, Ladakh Festival, Zanskar festival, and the Ladakh Marathon, the spokesperson said.

âThe marathon, in particular, attracts runners from across the country and beyond, with many participants travelling to Ladakh with their families, thereby generating wider benefits for hotels, homestays, restaurants, transport operators, guides, local businesses and other tourism-related services,â he added.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena attributed the growth to central govtâs sustained push for infrastructure development in Ladakh, as well as PM Narendra Modiâs appeal to citizens to visit locations in India and promote domestic tourism.

âThe fact that Ladakh has already crossed its entire 2025 tourist footfall in just eight months of this year is a very encouraging sign. Our focus, however, is not merely on increasing tourist numbers but on building a sustainable, responsible and year-round tourism economy that benefits our people,â Saxena said. Festivals, sporting events and cultural programmes are helping the region expand the tourism calendar beyond the traditional summer season and bring visitors to Ladakh during the shoulder and off seasons, he said.

World.title: Village head's appeal drove Ladakh LG's initiative to tap 90 million litres of glacial water for irrigation
World.content:
Village headâs appeal drove Ladakh LGâs initiative to tap 90 million litres of glacial water for irrigation

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Nearly 90 million litres of glacial water have started irrigating more than 1,000 acres of parched farmlands across 12 villages in Ladakh every day, thanks to a pioneering initiative by lieutenant governor (LG) V K Saxena last month.The massive volume of glacier-melt, previously flowing untapped into the River Indus, is now being channelised from Stok village nallah in Leh into the Igoo-Phey Irrigation Canal using simple earthwork that incurred little capital expenditure.It was an appeal from a village chief that drove the LG to brainstorm on harnessing glaciers and snowmelt for productive use. According to officials, Saxena was on a visit to Chuchot village in Leh where the âgobaâ (or nambardar, the traditional village head), Mirza Hussain, sought his intervention to address the acute water shortage in the village.The plea prompted the LG to spearhead a comprehensive and systematic campaign to identify locations where large volumes of glacial water were flowing down unused, draining straight into the Indus, even as surrounding farmlands remained dry, officials said.The govt first identified Stok village nallah, fed by the Stok Kangri Glacier, as one such place where glacier water could be diverted into the existing canal.Officials said the discharge from Stok nallah was assessed at 36 cusecs, or approximately 90 million litres of water in 24 hours.Two channels were then created to divert nearly 80 million litres of water into the Igoo-Phey Canal â 62 million litres toward Igoo village upstream and approximately 18 million litres toward Phey village downstream.This daily flow has substantially augmented the total water flow in the Igoo-Phey Canal â from 50 cusecs to nearly 90 cusecs. As a result, water supply will be guaranteed daily to the 12 villages fed by the canal. Previously, water from the 43-km-long Igoo-Phey Canal was distributed to villages on a restrictive roster basis due to limited availability.Having successfully channelised 80 million litres of water into the Igoo-Phey Canal, the remaining 10 million litres were diverted into another dry canal at Chuchot, and will help irrigate farmland in and around the village, officials said.âThe entire 90 million litres of water was tapped and the discharge from Stok Kangri glacier into the Indus River was reduced to zero in just two days at no cost,â said an official, adding that the success of the initiative serves as a blueprint for water management across the Union Territory.

World.title: NCPCR summons Meta India head over alleged child abuse ads
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has summoned Meta Indiaâs managing director and country head to appear before it on Wednesday over s allegedly linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) on Instagram.

The commission took suo motu cognisance of a BBC Eye report and issued a notice to Meta Platforms Inc on July 3, seeking an explanation and documents. Meta replied a week later, following which the NCPCR instituted a formal inquiry to establish the facts.

Commission officials remained tight-lipped about Metaâs response. However, officials said the inquiry would examine Meta Indiaâs role in the appearance of the s, how they cleared Instagramâs systems and why the situation arose.

The scrutiny would consider the stringent provisions relating to such material under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, they added.

Last week, the National Human Rights Commission issued notices to the ministry of electronics and information technology and ministry of information and broadcasting as part of its scrutiny of the alleged circulation of CSAM on Instagram. The Commission has given the ministries two weeks to give their response.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on September 2, said the inquiry was no longer limited to identifying who uploaded the objectionable content. âIt also examines the extent to which the platformâs own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content,â he said.

Meta had earlier said it had zero tolerance for child exploitation and had removed violating s and accounts. It also said its detection systems had led to the removal of more than 1.6 lakh suspicious accounts in India during the preceding six months. The company denied knowingly targeting such s at people displaying an inappropriate interest in children.

Queries sent to Meta on NCPCR summoning its top brass did not elicit a response.

World.title: Sri Lanka a close friend, India stands with it through thick and thin: Rajnath Singh
World.content:
Defence minister

said in Colombo on Tuesday that âIndia and Sri Lanka are close friends and India will always stand firmly with Sri Lanka whenever the island nation faces a crisis.â

Rajnath, who is on a three-day visit to Sri Lanka, has become the first Indian defence minister to arrive in the island nation for defence-level talks after nearly 40 years. The last time an Indian defence minister visited Sri Lanka for such talks was K C Pant, who visited the island nation in 1988.

âThe relationship between India and Sri Lanka is based on shared history, culture, and faith. We stand with Sri Lanka through thick and thin and are committed to the peace, prosperity, and development of both countries,â said Rajnath in Colombo as he began his maiden visit with an interaction with the Indian diaspora.

He asserted that both nations share close cultural and civilisational ties which have provided a strong foundation for the growth of the bilateral relationship.

âI am experiencing a sense of belonging after coming here,â he said while emphasising the importance of robust regional alliances. Rajnath highlighted Indiaâs expanding global influence and economic strength, and appreciated the work done by the Indian diaspora.





Before leaving for Colombo on Tuesday, Rajnath posted on X, âLooking forward to a productive engagement with the leadership of Sri Lanka during the visit. I shall also be interacting with the vibrant Indian diaspora in Sri Lanka. Besides our longstanding partnership as well as deep historical and civilisational ties, Sri Lanka is one of our most important partners under the âNeighbourhood Firstâ and âMAHASAGARâ initiatives.

â

Addressing the diaspora, Rajnath highlighted Indiaâs rapid economic transformation, stating that the country is among the fastest-growing major economies in the world and contributes more than 16% to global growth. He said that Indiaâs economy, which stood at $2 trillion in 2014, has doubled to approximately $4 trillion over the last decade. He added that amid global economic challenges, the countryâs economy grew at 7.8% in the first quarter of Financial Year (FY) 2026-27.

He also underlined the improvement in macroeconomic stability, saying that average inflation over the last 12 years has been approx. 4.7%, compared to 10-11% during the earlier period.

The minister pointed out that India has concluded trade deals with 38 countries over the last 12 years, including free trade agreements with eight major nations, compared to just four before 2014. Referring to the India-EU FTA as the âMother of All Dealsâ, he said the agreement opens access to the massive EU market and reflects Indiaâs growing diplomatic and economic capabilities.

He said that, compared to 12 years ago, the world today listens when India speaks on the international stage. World.title: NHRC seeks report on hostel facilities for DU students from Delhi chief secretary, UGC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Taking cognisance of the lack of adequate and affordable hostel facilities for students of the Delhi University, the National Human Rights Commission has issued directions to Delhi chief secretary and chairperson of the University Grants Commission to submit in consultation with DU a consolidated âaction-oriented reportâ within four weeks on the status of existing facilities, college-wise requirement, steps taken and the proposed plan with timelines for augmenting hostel accommodation.

The directions from the NHRC bench chaired by Priyank Kanoongo issued on September 7 gain significance as they come in the backdrop of the tragic building collapse in Satya Niketan area that has claimed lives of students.

In this latest directive, the commision has cited its September 30 notice from last year issued in response to a complaint by Network for Access to Justice and Multidisciplinary Outreach Foundation.

The non-profit had alleged that DU admits around 72,000 undergraduate students, but hostel availability was highly insufficient forcing students to take up expensive PGs or private rentals resulting in heavy financial burden and adverse impact on overall quality of life.

When Kanoongoâs bench had issued a notice last year seeking a report within two weeks from Delhi govt and ministry of education it first did not receive any response.





Only after a reminder went out warning of action that a report was received from Registrar (Colleges), Delhi University on Nov 11 .

The Commission has observed that the response does not adequately address the substantive grievance raised in the complaint and does not provide any concrete, coordinated or time-bound plan for addressing the shortage of hostel accommodation. Also no details on existing hostels and shortage of such facilities were provided to the commission.

In that report DU stated that funds for infrastructure enhancement, including augmentation of hostel facilities, are required to be provided by the funding agencies, namely the UGC and the Delhi govt and that the university and its colleges have been pursuing the matter with the respective funding agencies.

The University shared that students are admitted in undergraduate courses in 65 constituent/affiliated colleges; out of those, 12 colleges are 100% funded by the Delhi govt, while the remaining 53 colleges are funded wholly or substantially (100% or 95%) by the UGC.

The NHRC has, however, observed that the issue cannot remain confined to correspondence between the University, its colleges and their respective funding agencies and has called for coordinated consideration and action by the authorities responsible for funding and infrastructure.

World.title: Expelled Bihar Congress functionaries protest outside party office, seek meeting with Rahul
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A group of expelled Bihar Congress functionaries Tuesday protested in front of the party office here, and demanded a meeting with Rahul Gandhi so that they could âappriseâ him of the realities of the state unit.

The former Congress functionaries, led by Anand Madhab, were expelled for âanti-party activitiesâ after Bihar assembly elections. They had alleged irregularities in the selection of candidates and blamed AICC in-charge Krishna Allavaru and Bihar Congress chief Rajesh Kumar.

Madhab said their demands include an immediate appointment with Rahul, withdrawal of all disciplinary and expulsion proceedings and orders against them.

He also demanded removal of Allavaru and Kumar from their posts. Madhab said the process of restoration of faith in the party would start with the fulfilment of their demands. He said the leaders charged with indiscipline should be restored to their earlier positions in the organisation.

World.title: West Asia conflict LIVE: Iranian media says U.S. missile struck Iranian tanker off Kharg Island
World.content:
Iranian media on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) reported that a U.S. missile struck a tanker off the coast of Kharg Island, adding that there were no casualties.

“A small Iranian tanker was targeted by a missile attack by the American terrorist army four miles from Kharg Island. The tanker was hit by a projectile from American forces in the area of the Kharg Island anchorage,” Tasnim news agency said. The chief of staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, Ali Abdollahi, on Tuesday warned Tehran would attack U.S. bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers were hit.

The U.S. military said on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) that one of its underwater drones “malfunctioned” after Iran said its forces captured an American unmanned submarine in the strategic Strait of Hormuz. “An underwater drone operated by U.S. forces malfunctioned more than a day ago. It was surveying regional waters in support of ongoing operations,” U.S. Central Command spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins said, without mentioning whether the device was seized by Iran.

World.title: Chlorine gas leak at water filtration plant in Madhya Pradesh’s Sehore; four people hospitalised
World.content:
Chlorine gas leaked from a water filtration plant near the Kahiri Dam in Lasudia Khas village in Sehore district of Madhya Pradesh on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) night, affecting people in the vicinity, a police officer said.

Some people experienced eye irritation and breathing problems, and four of them were admitted to the Sehore District Hospital. According to doctors, all of them were out of danger.

Additional Superintendent of Police Prashant Choubey said a team of doctors, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel, and police has reached the spot.

The local administration was fully alert and, as a precaution, preparations are being made to secure the surrounding area to avoid any untoward incident, he said.

Chlorine gas was being used to purify water at the plant when a gas leak began from a tank, local sources claimed.

Mr. Choubey said that a team of doctors, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel, and police have reached the spot.

Local residents reported that chlorine gas was being used to purify the dam water at the plant when the gas leak began from a tank.

Senior doctor at the district hospital, Dr Hariom Gupta, said that no one was seriously injured and everyone is out of danger.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh rain forecast: showers from September 12 after a near 60% deficit
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh has recorded 59% less rain than normal this year, every one of its 28 districts is in deficit and the water table has sunk more than three metres in a year, State government data show. Heat has gripped much of the State, with day temperatures touching 42.2°C on Monday (September 7, 2026). Relief may come this weekend: the India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects a low-pressure system to form over the Bay of Bengal around September 11 and bring rain from September 12 to 15.

From January 1 to September 9, the State received 236.51 mm of rain against a normal of 578.58 mm, a shortfall of 59.12%, according to the Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Information and Management System (APWRIMS) dashboard. That places the State in the ‘deficient’ band, within a point of ‘scanty’, which begins at a 60% shortfall.

The southwest monsoon, which normally brings the bulk of the year’s rain, has fallen short in every month. From June 1 to September 9, the State received 209.45 mm against a normal of 462.51 mm, 54.71% below normal. July brought 51.69 mm against a normal of 161.07 mm, 68% short; August 73.16 mm against 165.78 mm, 56% short; and the first nine days of this month 9.11 mm against 35.43 mm, 74% short.

Seven districts ‘scanty’

Seven districts have slipped into the ‘scanty’ band for the year. Annamayya is the driest, at 79.75 mm against a normal of 388.32 mm, a shortfall of 79.46%. Prakasam is 72.88% short, Visakhapatnam 68.43%, Chittoor 67.56%, West Godavari 61.10%, East Godavari 60.93% and Kakinada 60.15%. None of the 28 is in the normal or excess band. By region, Rayalaseema is 59.08% short and Coastal Andhra 55.91%. Counted from June 1 alone, six districts are scanty: Annamayya, Prakasam, Chittoor, Sri Sathya Sai, Visakhapatnam and Markapuram.

Water table

The State’s average groundwater level stood at 11.37 metres below ground on Wednesday (September 9, 2026), against 8.28 metres on the same date last year, a fall of 3.09 metres, state government data shows. The table has dropped 1.27 metres since May, through the monsoon months, and 5.36 metres since November. In Rayalaseema the average is 14.41 metres below ground, 4.82 metres deeper than a year ago; in Coastal Andhra it is 10.15 metres, 2.40 metres deeper. Of the 26 districts in the state, West Godavari is the lone exception: its table is 7.74 metres below ground, two centimetres higher than last year.

Sri Sathya Sai’s average has dropped to 21.19 metres below ground from 11.05 metres a year ago, a fall of 10.14 metres; Annamayya’s to 18.22 metres from 11.15 metres, a fall of 7.07 metres; and Ananthapuramu’s to 15.98 metres from 10.52 metres, a fall of 5.46 metres. Eluru has the deepest table in the State at 23.87 metres, 4.98 metres lower than last year, followed by East Godavari at 22.94 metres and Markapuram at 21.63 metres.

Heat and the forecast

The mercury touched 42.2°C at Throvagunta in Ongole and at Venkatagiri in Tirupati district on Monday (September 7), according to the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES). Pottempadu in Nellore district recorded 41.8°C, and Karamchedu in Bapatla 41.7°C. In all, 94 stations in the State recorded 40°C or more on Monday. On Tuesday too, temperatures hovered around 40°C; at 5 p.m., Palagiri in YSR Kadapa district, and Chintavaram and Kandaleru in Nellore district recorded 37.7°C.

Both maximum and minimum temperatures have stayed above normal for two days, the IMD said. S. Karunasagar, senior scientist at IMD-Amaravati, said temperatures were rising because of the lack of rainfall under the El Niño effect and unfavourable conditions for convection. “This means no clouds, no moisture and hence, dry weather,” he said.

An upper-air cyclonic circulation lies over the west-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining coastal Andhra Pradesh at 7.6 km above mean sea level, the IMD said, and may intensify into a low-pressure area near north coastal Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha around September 11. Hot and humid weather may persist in coastal Andhra Pradesh till then, after which light to moderate showers are expected across the State, with isolated heavy rainfall in north coastal Andhra Pradesh from September 12 to 15.

World.title: HC seeks Delhi govt.’s action plan to eliminate rabies in stray dogs
World.content:
The High Court on Tuesday asked the Delhi government to submit its response on implementing the action plan for elimination of rabies in stray dogs in the national capital.

The court also asked the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) to submit their status reports on steps taken by them to vaccinate and sterilise stray dogs.

During the hearing, a Bench of Justice Dinesh Mehta and Justice Rajneesh Kumar Gupta was informed that the amicus curiae, appointed to assist the court in the matter, has prepared an action plan for dog-mediated rabies elimination from India by 2030.

The court was informed that the MCD held four camps in Anand Vihar ward in August and September during which 43 dogs were caught, sterilised and vaccinated and released to their respective areas.

The court was also informed that NDMC also conducted camps during which 28 dogs were caught, 615 dogs were vaccinated and school awareness programmes were held.

The court directed that the MCD and NDMC mention in their status reports as to how many dogs were caught and also ensure that at least one ward from their areas is rabies-free.

The authorities submitted that they will continue holding the camps and will make at least one ward rabies-free and that all dogs will be vaccinated and sterilised.

The court listed the matter for further hearing on October 5.

The Bench passed the order on a suo motu case initiated by the court pursuant to the Supreme Court’s directions passed on May 19. The SC had directed the State governments and Union Territories to augment infrastructure to deal with stray dogs and other animals, and asked all the High Courts to register a suo motu case to ensure compliance of its August 22, 2025, and November 7, 2025, directions.

World.title: INDIA bloc parties announce Odisha Assembly ‘gherao’ on Sept. 29 over new mining law
World.content:
Political parties belonging to INDIA Bloc on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) called for statewide campaign and besieging Odisha Legislative Assembly on September 29 demanding protection of the State’s rights over mineral resources, the land, forest and livelihood rights of tribals.

The INDIA bloc in Odisha on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) called for a Statewide campaign and ‘gherao’ of the Assembly on September 29, demanding the protection of the State’s rights over its mineral resources, land and forests.

At a convention attended by the constituent parties of the coalition group, including the Congress, Communist Party of India (CPI), Communist Party of India (Marxist), Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist) Liberation, All India Forward Bloc, Nationalist Congress Party, Samajwadi Party and Rashtriya Janata Dal, speakers alleged the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, undermined the constitutional and fiscal rights of the States and provided greater scope for the exploitation of mineral resources by corporate entities.

Linking Odisha’s taxation and revenue-raising powers over mineral resources with Central approval was a “serious assault on the State’s fiscal autonomy”, they said.

“The historic Supreme Court judgment of 2024 recognised the constitutional rights of States in relation to mineral resources and their power to levy taxes on lands containing mineral resources,” said CPI(M) State secretary Suresh Panigrahi.

INDIA bloc leaders also alleged that mineral-rich States like Odisha stand to lose enormous revenues, running into lakhs of crores of rupees with the Centre preventing the recovery of previously uncollected taxes, cess and arrears.

Declaring that the State’s mineral resources belong to the people of Odisha, the convention presided by Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee president Bhakta Charan Das called for the repeal of the new Act, protection of the State’s constitutional rights, safeguarding the land, forest and livelihood rights of tribals, and the building of a broad-based people’s movement against “corporate plunder”.

“The convention also called for a mass mobilisation against the mining policies of the BJP government. A State Assembly gherao will be organised on September 29 as part of the continuing struggle,” said Mr. Panigrahi.

The book, Modi’s Blueprint for Mining Loot, authored by senior Left leader Santosh Das, was also formally released at the political convention.

World.title: Bone-sparing hip procedure performed on two international patients
World.content:
Doctors of SIMS Hospital performed a bone-sparing hip procedure on two international patients.

The two patients — one aged 44 from the U.S. and another aged 58 from the U.K. — underwent the procedures. Both looked up for hip resurfacing options as they wanted to be active and athletic.

According to a press release, while the conventional hip procedures often require extensive removal of bone, this approach preserves a substantial portion of the patient’s healthy natural bone while achieving a stable and functional reconstruction.

Vijay C. Bose, joint director and senior consultant, Orthopaedics, said the hip joint is a ball and socket joint. The joint can become arthritic or damaged. He said that hip resurfacing is a bone-preserving procedure. Patients had access to hip resurfacing through metal-on-metal implants but these had certain issues and were largely discontinued worldwide.

“As a result, patients could not access hip resurfacing procedures. We now have an implant made of high density polyethylene that has been launched in Tamil Nadu. This helps in conserving the bone, shape and anatomy, and facilitates high activity including competitive sports,” he explained.

The goal was not simply to replace a painful joint but to preserve as much of the patient’s own bone as possible while respecting the natural mechanics of the hip, he said, according to the release.

Ravi Pachamuthu, chairman of SRM Group, said that India and Tamil Nadu were growing as a medical hub. Raju Sivasamy, vice president, SIMS Hospital and Sharat Kusuma, Chief Executive Officer of Joint Medica USA along with the two patients were present.

World.title: Monthly assistance for ex-servicemen, widows to be raised to ₹6,000, says Minister
World.content:
Minister for Non-Resident Tamil Welfare K. Thennarasu on Tuesday announced in the Assembly that the monthly assistance for ex-servicemen and their widows would be increased from ₹4,000 to ₹6,000.

Making the announcements for the Public Department, Mr. Thennarasu said an AI-enabled chatbot and an interactive voice bot would be introduced on the Mudhalvarin Mugavari website at a cost of ₹2.18 crore. Digital kiosks would be installed at the Secretariat and Collectorates to enable the public to access government services.

He also said the monthly cash assistance for Sri Lankan Tamils living in camps would be enhanced to ₹1,800 for the head of the family, ₹1,200 for family members aged above 12 and ₹600 for those aged below 12. The educational assistance provided to children of Sri Lankan Tamils living in camps would be increased by ₹2,000.

He said the State government would institute the ‘Vettri Tamilar Award’ to honour non-resident Tamils who had rendered significant support and assistance for the welfare of Tamils abroad.

Minister for Finance N. Marie Wilson, while making announcements for the Planning and Development Department, said a Health Research Centre would be established in the State Planning Commission to provide policy advice and guidance to the government.

He also said an Evidence-based Government Unit, in collaboration with the Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency, would be established to enable the government to make and implement decisions based on evidence.

World.title: Raghav Chadha’s name added in Delhi electoral
World.content:
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Tuesday alleged irregularities behind the addition of BJP MP Raghav Chadha’s name in Delhi’s voter list even as poll officials rejected claims of any irregularities. Chadha’s name was included in the electoral rolls of the Rajinder Nagar Assembly constituency.

Addressing a press conference, AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj said, “The Election Commission committing ‘farziwada’ (fraud) is nothing new... When the SIR process is underway and there were 746 voters in the booth in the draft roll, through what process did Raghav Chadha become the 747th voter?”

The office of Delhi Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), in a statement, said: “25,011 Form 6 applications had been submitted between August 31 and September 7 and that these, along with the earlier applications, are “under process”. Once approved, the addition is reflected in the electoral database. However, the actual addition to the electoral roll is to be published in the supplementary electoral roll on November 4.”

The draft electoral rolls for Delhi were published on August 31. On September 3, Chadha’s name was deleted from Punjab’s draft roll, following which he had stated that he would get his vote registered again in Punjab, from where he was sent to the Rajya Sabha by his previous party AAP.

Mr. Chadha said in a statement, “I seem to be haunting Arvind Kejriwal and the Aam Aadmi Party. I have followed all applicable ECI guidelines and procedures and availed the prescribed remedies.”

World.title: Govt hikes petrol price by Rs5.58, HSD by Rs4.18
World.content:
The government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol by Rs5.58 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.18 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs364.35 per litre while HSD will cost Rs385.95 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 9 (Wednesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: PM Shehbaz seeks input from business community as he stresses export-led growth
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday sought recommendations from industrialists and businesspeople on how to increase export-led growth in the country.

“Whatever growth we have to achieve, it has to be export-led growth, period,” the premier remarked while addressing a meeting with prominent leaders of the business community.

He added that any other kind of growth had “no meaning” and reinforced that economic growth had to be export-led.

“Today’s meeting is because we’re in the first quarter, in the month of September. I need your opinions on how to increase our exports, as well as what challenges we will face and how to address them,” PM Shehbaz said.

The prime minister gave the example of special tax relief to exporters as a means to achieve this growth.

He recalled that in the run-up to the federal budget presented in June this year, the government held multiple meetings and had “intense consultations” with the business community.

“Through your consultations in difficult times, the way we brought structural changes over the past two-and-a-half years … it’s teamwork. It’s a tremendous teamwork,” PM Shehbaz said.

“As a result, we made overdue structural reforms. It’s a long journey, but through enforcement we recovered Rs800 billion in one year. No new taxes were imposed.”

PM Shehbaz praised the teamwork involved between the business community and the government, adding that Pakistan was ready to pursue growth with their input.

In July, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the government was pursuing a strategy to diversify exportable products and market portfolios to achieve a target of six per cent sustainable economic growth.

“Our destination is not only stabilisation but sustainable growth of at least 6pc. That growth has to be export-led; otherwise it will become another economic bubble that bursts within a few years,” he said.

Last Monday, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said that the government’s focus was on building an ecosystem to support sustainable growth that was led by the private sector and export-driven.

The minister said Pakistan had moved from stabilisation towards growth, but the key challenge now was to ensure its sustainability.

Earlier this week, PM Shehbaz welcomed the launch of export insurance coverage by the Export Development Fund (EDF) and the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan, saying the facility would help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) expand the country’s exports.

Chairing a meeting on the EDF, he said the Rs3bn risk pool would expand access to export credit insurance, especially for SMEs, and help the business community increase export volumes.

He described the initiative as a highly welcome step to promote small and medium-sized businesses and strengthen the national economy.

World.title: Sindh AG interrupts Mir Raza commission proceedings during police surgeon's testimony, objects to family's queries
World.content:
KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to probe the circumstances and possible negligence around the Mir Raza Ali murder case issued notice to Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar after the Sindh Advocate General Jawad Dero interrupted the proceedings on Tuesday and objected to the lawyer representing the victims’ family asking any questions.

The interruption came during Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed’s testimony.

The order issued after the commission’s proceedings stated: “It is regrettable that the commission’s proceedings have been interrupted by Sindh Advocate General Jawad Dero. He has objected to the family’s counsel asking any questions on behalf of the deceased’s family.

“The highest law officer of the Sindh government making such a submission surprised me. It is more meaningful that the disturbance comes at a time when the police surgeon was explaining the role of senior police officers during the post-mortem examination.”

The murder case has been mired in controversy, particularly after Dr Syed pointed out flaws in the findings of Ali’s first autopsy. Following that, Ali’s body was exhumed a second post-mortem was conducted.

Dr Syed was part of the medical board that conducted the second autopsy, whose findings ruled out the possibility of suicide — a likelihood around which the law enforcers had initially tried to build the case. Meanwhile, Ali’s family accused police of trying to bury the facts.

The one-member commission, headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, heard the case today and noted in its order that Sindh Assembly member Faryal Talpur had suggested its formation to the provincial chief executive “for a transparent and impartial comprehensive investigation”.

The order cited a Dawn report dated Aug 9, according to which, it said, Talpur stressed that justice for Ali must be ensured and “public should be transparently informed of all facts surrounding the case. The newspaper further cites her as saying that providing justice to the bereaved family and maintaining public confidence in the justice system was the fundamental responsibility of the government and relevant institutions”.

Sindh Home Minister Lanjar and Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah had echoed these sentiments, the order stated.

Justice Sial further wrote in the order that he was saddened that the advocate general had objected to requests by Ali’s family through their counsel for certain clarification.

“It is the commission’s discretion to determine whether a query is relevant to the proceedings or not. Further, the commission’s terms of reference required it to find the true facts and circumstances of the case,” he said, adding that a notice was being issued to Lanjar to appear before the commission on Sept 10 and “put forward his stance […] as to whether the family is barred from asking questions to satisfy themselves that justice is being done”.

Justice Sial further stated, “In my opinion, a deliberate attempt has been made by the Sindh advocate general to restrain the commission from addressing the family’s queries in a transparent manner.”

Plea against FIR

In a separate development, a two-member bench of the SHC, headed by Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar and including Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri, took up a petition seeking the quashing of a case registered on August 27 against “around 100 people” for staging a protest in connection with the case.

In the first information report (FIR), the protesters have been accused of blocking the road for vehicular movement and pedestrians at Karachi’s Sharea Faisal.

The plea, a copy of which is available with Dawn, named Ammar Ahmed Khan, Muhammad Zubai Ali, Taha Shaikh, Zarar Khalid, Saad Shehriyar, and Hassan Surya as the petitioners.

The SHC issued notices to the Sindh advocate general, the prosecutor general and other respondents for Nov 11 after hearing the plea today, directing that in the meantime, no coercive action should be taken against the petitioners.

The court further directed that the investigation should be conducted strictly in accordance with the law and directed the petitioners to cooperate when required.

“It is clarified that this order shall not be construed as an impediment in conducting the investigation strictly in accordance with law,” the court said.

The case so far

The body of 25-year-old Ali was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28.

Days after the recovery of Ali’s body on July 29, Dr Syed had told Geo News that the post-mortem findings in the case had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

On August 6, a Karachi court took up an application by Ali’s father, allowed the exhumation of his body, ordered the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose and directed that a second autopsy of Ali’s body be conducted.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir, accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8.

A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered under charges of kidnapping.

The order for the probe team’s reconstitution also showed that a murder charge had been added to the first information report.

The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team.

On Aug 19, Ali’s parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam Hussain, wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, seeking his “direct supervision of the murder investigation”. They also urged the chief minister to order an investigation and departmental inquiry into the previous investigation team and immediately suspend the officers involved.

The provincial government acknowledged the letter and announced the decision on Aug 23 to form a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and to investigate the circumstances surrounding Ali’s death.

However, soon after the announcement, the counsel for Ali’s family raised objections and later approached the Sindh High Court (SHC).

The petition was filed on August 24 in objection to the provincial government’s decision to form a judicial commission and sought the formation of an independent and multi-agency JIT “comprising officers who have had no previous involvement in the case” in place of the commission.

On Sept 2, the SHC dismissed a petition filed by Ali’s family, seeking the formation of a JIT to probe his murder, observing that constituting such a body was the “prerogative of the government”.

Meanwhile, the final report of Ali’s second post-mortem for the Mir Raza Ali murder case confirmed that his death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back.

“Death occurred due to cardiac rupture consequent to perforating firearm injury of the chest,” the report stated, adding that the entry wound was on the posterior thorax (back) and the exit wound on the anterior thorax (front of the chest).

“The findings are inconsistent with suicide as the manner of death,” it confirmed.

World.title: HRW cautions against normalising ties with Taliban amid rights concerns
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has warned countries against normalising engagement with the Taliban without clear and measurable human rights benchmarks, as a UN expert highlighted the devastating consequences of five years of Taliban rule for Afghan children and young people.

“Countries should not normalise engagement with the Taliban without clear and measurable human rights benchmarks,” HRW said in a statement to the UN Human Rights Council on Monday.

It urged states to recognise gender apartheid as a crime against humanity and support International Criminal Court (ICC) efforts to prosecute those responsible for gender persecution and other grave international crimes in Afghanistan.

The warning came as Richard Bennett, the UN special rapporteur on the human rights situation in Afghanistan, issued a new report on the impact of Taliban policies on children.

Bennett said the Taliban’s institutionalised system of discrimination, repression and ideological control was depriving children of their rights to inclusive and quality education, freedom of expression and meaningful participation in social and public life.

“Afghanistan’s children are growing up in an environment where discrimination, especially against girls and women, is being normalised; they are denied the right to learn and their opportunities for the future are dramatically shrinking,” Bennett said.

He expressed particular concern over the continued denial of education beyond the sixth grade to girls and the growing exposure of children and young people to gender-based violence, forced and child marriage, child labour and ideological indoctrination.

“These policies are not only violating children’s rights today — they are undermining their ability to determine their own futures,” Bennett said.

“For girls in particular, the systematic denial of education is closing doors that may never reopen, with serious consequences for their mental health and the country’s development as a whole.”

The report said these abuses were taking place against a backdrop of decades of conflict, poverty and unmet humanitarian needs. By dismantling or weakening institutions that previously protected children’s rights, the Taliban had exposed Afghan children to greater risks of violence, abuse and exploitation, Bennett said.

Children living in poverty or remote areas, those with disabilities, members of marginalised religious and ethnic communities, and displaced children or those returning from abroad are among the most vulnerable, he said.

Bennett also warned that restrictions on media, culture and freedom of expression were limiting the diversity of ideas and experiences available to Afghan children.

“Children need space to learn, to think freely, to express themselves and imagine a different future,” he said. “Instead, many are growing up in fear, isolation and uncertainty.”

The restrictions, combined with limited educational opportunities, were contributing to a growing sense of despair and could create future security concerns and a migration crisis, Bennett warned.

He cautioned, however, against viewing Afghan children only as victims, noting their resilience and determination to support their families and communities and pursue alternative forms of learning.

Bennett urged the Taliban to end discriminatory policies, restore comprehensive education for girls, strengthen child protection and justice systems, prevent child and forced marriage and child labour, prohibit corporal punishment, and restore inclusive healthcare and social protection for children with disabilities.

He also called on other countries to fully fund humanitarian assistance, expand alternative education for girls and safe pathways for Afghans at risk, and support mine-action programmes, youth initiatives and international accountability efforts.

“Five years of restrictive rule and socio-economic collapse have fundamentally altered the conditions in which Afghanistan’s children are growing up,” Bennett said.

“The international community must act now to protect their rights and ensure that present and future generations are not deprived of the opportunity to shape Afghanistan’s future.”

HRW, meanwhile, said gender persecution had become further entrenched over the past year, with the Taliban dismantling already limited legal protections for women and girls.

“Since 2021, Taliban authorities have systematically deprived women and girls of their fundamental rights,” the organisation said.

HRW cited a new criminal procedure code that recognises only “excessive” beating as domestic violence against women, potentially leaving survivors of other forms of abuse without effective avenues for justice. It also said a decree concerning judicial separation had eliminated minimum-age protections for girls’ marriage.

Journalists, human rights defenders, peaceful protesters and former government employees continue to face arbitrary detention, enforced disappearance, torture and other serious abuses, HRW said.

The organisation urged UN member states to renew Bennett’s mandate and provide his office with the resources needed to independently monitor and report on Afghanistan. It also called for the urgent operationalisation of the Human Rights Council’s new independent accountability mechanism for the country.

HRW further urged governments not to forcibly return people to Afghanistan, where persecution remains systematic and well documented, and to support efforts by the International Criminal Court to prosecute those responsible for gender persecution and other grave international crimes.

“Afghan victims, survivors and their families have waited far too long for truth, justice, and reparation,” HRW said.

Separately, UN Secretary-General António Guterres renewed his call on the Taliban to lift restrictions preventing Afghan women working for the UN from entering its premises and carrying out their duties.

The UN has said the restrictions hamper its ability to deliver assistance and services to the Afghan population, particularly women and girls.

The warnings from Bennett, HRW and Guterres come as the Taliban regime approaches five years in power, with the UN expert warning that its policies are affecting not only the rights of Afghans today but the prospects of an entire generation of children.

World.title: Babar says was surprised by PCB’s decision to sack Sarfraz, send seven players home
World.content:
The Pakistan Cricket Board’s (PCB) decision to sack the national team’s head coach and send seven players back home following the defeat against England at Lord’s last week came as a surprise to captain Babar Azam, he revealed on Tuesday.

The 194-run drubbing — which sealed the three-match series for the hosts — was followed by Sarfraz Ahmed’s removal as Pakistan’s head coach and Umar Gul’s dismissal as bowling coach. They were replaced by white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke, respectively.

Seven players, including seasoned campaigners Imam-ul-Haq, Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Ali Agha, were axed from the squad midway through the series, while five of the replacements flown to the UK were uncapped players.

The wholesale changes, as it emerged later, were planned outside the Pakistan dressing room by the national selection panel. As was the case with most members of the team’s contingent, the developments came as a surprise to Babar as well.

“It was news to me as well,” Babar said during the pre-match press conference ahead of the final Test at Edgbaston. “I only found out about these things later.”

Following the PCB’s dramatic move, the board’s high-performance director and selector Aaqib Javed revealed that the decision to sack the coaching staff was a reaction to their inability to make certain selection calls ahead of the second Test.

While Sarfraz and Umar bore the brunt of the PCB’s action, Babar was retained to lead the side in the final Test. The captain, however, distanced himself from the board’s decisions.

Pakistan’s Azan Awais during practice ahead of the third Test match against England at Edgbaston, Birmingham, England on September 7, 2026. — Reuters

“But as I said, the PCB made the decisions, so I think they would be better placed to explain them,” he said. “Whatever decision the PCB has taken, as a player and as captain, I have to go along with the decision made by the cricket board.

“…The PCB would have made its decision after giving it considerable thought.

“In my opinion, it would be better to ask them about it because they would be able to explain it much better.”

Babar also gave a straight “no” when asked whether he was aware of the PCB’s internal inquiry into the discipline and conduct of certain players.

Nothing to lose

Babar and his players have little option but to put a tumultuous week behind them and focus on what they can produce on the field. To do so, however, he and Hesson have a number of fresh faces to choose from.

The uncapped duo of pacer Razaullah and all-rounder Arafat Minhas could make their debuts, while Saim Ayub — who has eight Tests to his name — is likely to return to the side.

Babar described the situation as an opportunity for the young players amid the chaos.

England’s Jamie Smith during practice ahead of the third Test match against England at Edgbaston, Birmingham, England on September 7, 2026. — Reuters

“…The new players are coming in, and they have a golden opportunity to grab it and play this game,” he said, adding that the final Test, being a dead rubber, could help Pakistan handle the pressure better.

“For us, this is an opportunity as a team and as a group. The series is lost, but we have nothing to lose. So we can play freely, go out onto the ground and believe in ourselves as a team,” he added.

“We have had a couple of days of practice and have spoken to each other a lot. Whenever a new team or a youngster comes in, there is a little excitement, and that excitement is visible.”

World.title: Three held after Karachi University professor assaulted at Safoora Chowrangi
World.content:
KARACHI: Police on Tuesday arrested three suspects after a senior faculty member of the University of Karachi and his nephew were allegedly assaulted with pistol butts following a minor traffic accident near Safoora Chowrangi, police said.

East Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Zubair Nazir Sheikh told Dawn that the victims were University of Karachi’s Islamic Learning Department chairman Dr Professor Mohammed Arif Khan Saqi and his nephew, Mohammed Waheed Rehman.

“The professor was travelling along a main road on his way to the university, while the suspects were reversing their vehicle when it hit his,” SSP Sheikh said.

He said the police had given the professor a letter for medico-legal formalities, following which a first information report (FIR) was registered at Sachal police station.

“The police conducted raids and arrested three suspects. Further efforts were under way to arrest the remaining suspects,” he added.

Sachal police station House Officer (SHO) Aijaz Pathan told Dawn that the suspects were influential persons who owned a restaurant in Safoora. He said raids were being conducted to arrest all those involved in the incident.

Meanwhile, the FIR, registered on a complaint by Dr Saqi, invoked sections 147 (punishment for rioting), 148 (rioting while armed with a deadly weapon), 149 (every member of an unlawful assembly guilty of an offence committed in prosecution of the common object), 324 (attempt to commit qatl-i-amd) and 342 (punishment for wrongful confinement) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

According to the complainant, he was travelling with his nephew in a car to the University of Karachi when the incident occurred.

“When we reached Safoora Chowrangi near Green Hotel at around 10:15am, a double-cabin vehicle hit and damaged the bonnet of our car and attempted to drive away,” Dr Saqi said.

He said the situation escalated when he asked the occupants of the vehicle to compensate for the damage to his car.

Dr Saqi added that when he asked for their names, the suspects exited the vehicle and started assaulting his nephew.

“In the meantime, their gunmen also arrived and started beating my nephew and me; as a result, we both fell on the road after being injured.”

Later on, the suspects forcibly took them to a nearby eatery, the complainant said, adding that they were beaten again before the suspects fled.

World.title: UK's Miliband announces sanctions on goods from West Bank over 'ethnic cleansing' by Israeli settlers
World.content:
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Tuesday accused the Israeli government of turning a “blind eye” to what he called “ethnic cleansing” by settlers in the West Bank.

In a video statement, he called the situation in Palestine a “moral emergency” and said that there is increasing evidence of war crimes in Gaza.

“We are witnessing unprecedented settler terrorism in the West Bank,” he said.

“The British government has come to the same conclusion as the former prime minister of Israel and others, that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank, perpetrated by settler terrorists.”

He noted that Tel Aviv had not only ignored these developments, but that members and officials had made statements or taken actions enabling the forced displacement of Palestinians.

“We will not stand by. We’re going to be stronger in standing up for what is right, and bolder in the action we take,” Miliband said, adding that London’s north star was the two-state solution.

“Today, we are calling out the occupation of Palestine as unlawful,” he added.

“We are banning the import of goods from illegal settlements, we’re taking action on services to target those who finance, facilitate or construct new settlements, and we’re banning s of settlement properties and land.”

In parliament today, Miliband said the British government would introduce “an import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories”, in a move coordinated with other countries.

“The British government agrees that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank, perpetrated by settler terrorists,” said Miliband.

He also announced that Britain would “take action against specific companies and individuals who provide services such as construction, infrastructure, financing, or real estate for settlement expansion” and that the measures would be in place within six to nine months.

Miliband added that the UK was sanctioning “a further set of extremist settlers who have supported or incited acts of violence against Palestinian communities”.

Miliband, the son of Jewish refugees to Britain, said he was “proud” of his Jewish heritage and was “unwavering” in his support of Israel.

“There is absolutely no contradiction between this and my support for the State of Palestine,” he added.

US will not join sanctions on Israeli settlements

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the United States will not join the UK-led sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements, and that it does not want anything to destabilise the West Bank.

“Obviously, we’re not going to do what the UK did,” Rubio told journalists about the sanctions before departing on a trip to Latin America, adding: “We don’t want to see anything destabilising going on right now in the West Bank with so much going on in the region.”

UK, France among 12 countries sanctioning Israeli settlements

Twelve countries, including the UK, Canada and France, said they would slap sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, after increasing attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the occupied territory.

Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, and Sweden also plan to limit trade with the settlements, the nations’ foreign ministers said in a joint statement.

Ireland and Spain have already taken measures against trade with Israeli settlements, and France has for weeks been pushing for a similar decision from the European Union, Israel’s leading trading partner, but has been blocked by some members.

“The government of Israel’s actions in the West Bank are undermining the possibility of a two-state solution,” the 12 ministers said, referring to a plan under which two states — one Israeli and one Palestinian — would live peacefully side by side.

Israeli soliders gather during a military operation after a Palestinian man barricaded himself inside a home in the Israel-occupied West Bank village of Aqraba, south of the city of Nablus, in the occupied West Bank on September 8, 2026. — AFP

“The situation is rapidly deteriorating amid unprecedented levels of settler violence and settlement expansion,” they warned.

“The government of Israel must immediately halt the expansion of settlements and civilian administrative powers, ensure accountability for settler violence, and investigate allegations against Israeli forces.”

The ministers said the 12 countries “confirm their intention to introduce national and/or support European restrictions on trade in goods with settlements which are illegal under international law, or that they are actively considering these and other measures, in accordance with their national procedures.”

Israeli court rejects petition to halt key settlement project

An Israeli court rejected a bid from rights groups to halt the development of a settlement in the occupied West Bank that would severely undermine the territorial contiguity of a future Palestinian state.

The Jerusalem District Court said in a ruling it had dismissed the motion, which aimed to stall the publication of tenders for the settlement east of Jerusalem.

Israel’s construction and housing ministry opened a tender for construction of more than 1,200 housing units in July, leading NGOs to file motions against it.

An image taken from the Israeli-occupied West Bank village of Aqraba shows the the new illegal Israeli outpost (C) being built on Palestinian land and sandwiched between Aqraba and Jurish (on the hill), south of the West Bank city of Nablus on September 8, 2026. — AFP

The E1 plan — approved by Israel last year after decades of being frozen, notably due to pressure from successive US administrations — would further isolate Israeli-occupied east Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank. Six European countries, including the UK and France, called on Israel to halt the project in August.

The Israeli judge ruled that “no irreversible physical changes are imminent, and adequate legal safeguards are in place” for the development project, arguing that courts could bring a permanent ruling on the project as a whole, well before physical construction begins on the ground.

The petitioners, including Israeli NGO Peace Now, had argued that the project would lead to the eviction of hundreds of Palestinians.

“The court’s decision plays into the government’s hands, allowing it to use the final months of its term to establish facts on the ground that will create a destructive reality which will be extremely difficult to reverse,” the NGOs said in a statement reacting to the ruling.

World.title: PMDC instructs medical, dental colleges not to admit Afghan students for 'current academic session'
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) has barred medical and dental colleges from granting admission or placement to Afghan students for the current academic session, and students previously enrolled in such programmes are “required to return to Afghanistan”, Dawn has learnt.

The policy decision was conveyed by the council to public and private medical institutions across the country earlier this month.

The PMDC communique, seen by Dawn, dated Sept 1, 2026, calls on all institutions to ensure the completion of administrative formalities to facilitate the departure of Afghan students.

“It is further reiterated that Afghan nationals previously enrolled in medical or dental programs in Pakistan are required to return to Afghanistan, in accordance with the prevailing policy directions,” said the PMDC communique.

“The concerned institutions shall ensure that all necessary administrative formalities, including issuance of requisite NOCs and facilitation of their departure are completed, accordingly,” added the council.

The development came amid reports, circulating on social media, about the alleged expulsion of Afghan nationals who were studying at public sector medical colleges in Lahore.

According to a health ministry official, an “in principle” decision had been made to send Afghan students enrolled in Pakistani medical universities back to their country, due to the ongoing tensions between Islamabad and Kabul.

“Letters have been written to all medical universities asking their constituent colleges about the number of Afghan nationals enrolled in medical and dental colleges. Universities have also been directed to provide details of how many students are studying in each year,” he explained.

The official said the PMDC had details of most Afghan medical students; however, “there remained a possibility that some may have been missed or mistakenly identified as nationals of other countries or as locals”.

“After getting the information, lists will be shared with the concerned quarters, and the rest will be decided by them,” he said.

However, he also clarified that the decision did not apply to students of other nationalities, only Afghan students.

When asked about the reported expulsion of Afghan students, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan told Dawn: “As per the Illegal Foreigner Repatriation Plan (IFRP), stay of any foreign national without a valid visa and passport is illegal, and the concerned individual is liable to deportation.”

Khan added that Pakistani authorities were continuing to process visa extension applications from Afghan students “in line with our existing policy, rules and regulations”.

The vice chancellor of a medical university confirmed receipt of the PMDC instructions, saying that institutions had begun collecting Afghan students’ particulars in line with the council’s instructions.

“There were a number of students enrolled in undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. Although we were directed to provide the data, we were not told why such action was being taken,” he said.

Millions of Afghans have poured into Pakistan over the past several decades, fleeing successive wars, including hundreds of thousands who arrived after the Taliban returned to power in 2021.

In June, the Ministry of Interior issued a directive to immediately arrest any Afghan national “found residing in Pakistan without a valid visa” from July 10.

A deportation drive first launched in 2023 was renewed in April last year when the government rescinded hun­dreds of thousands of residence permits for Afghans, warning them of arrests if they did not leave.

Last year alone, over a million Afghan nationals were deported by Pakistan, a Senate Standing Committee on Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and States and Frontier Regions (SAFRON) was informed.

Pakistan deported a total of 1,155,221 Afghan nationals in 2025, top officials of the Ministry of Interior and Chief Commissionerate for Afghan Refugees told the meeting.

The repatriation push also comes as relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have deteriorated. Pakistan has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban government to rein in terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan and prevent militant groups from carrying out attacks against Pakistan from Afghan soil. However, its appeals have gone unheeded.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.
